title: 708. The Terror: The Reign of Robespierre (Part 2)

sentences.en: We are now, therefore, got to that black precipitous abyss, where all things have long been tending, where, having now arrived on the giddy verge, they hurl down in confused ruin,
sentences.zh: 因此，我们现在来到了那个黑色的险峻深渊，一切事物长期以来都在向这里靠拢，而今它们已经抵达了摇摇欲坠的边缘，在混乱的废墟中轰然下坠，

sentences.en: headlong, pell-mell, down, down, till sans-culottism have consummated itself.
sentences.zh: 头朝下，混乱不堪，坠落，坠落，直到无裤党主义彻底完成其历史使命。

sentences.en: And in this wondrous French Revolution, as in a doomsday, a world have been rapidly, if not born again, yet destroyed and engulfed.
sentences.zh: 在这场奇妙的法国大革命中，如同面临末日审判，世界即使没有重生，也被迅速摧毁并吞没。

sentences.en: Terror has long been terrible, but to the actors themselves, it has now become manifest that their appointed course is one of terror.
sentences.zh: 恐怖统治早已令人胆寒，但对于行动者自身而言，他们现在也逐渐明了，他们注定要走上一条恐怖之路。

sentences.en: And they say, be it so, que la terreur soit l'ordre du jour.
sentences.zh: 他们说，那就这样吧，让恐怖成为当务之急。

sentences.en: Let terror be the order of the day.
sentences.zh: 让恐怖成为当务之急。

sentences.en: So, what a dramatic moment, a key point in the story of the French Revolution, the start of the terror.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一个多么戏剧性的时刻，法国大革命故事中的一个关键节点，恐怖统治的开端。

sentences.en: So, this passage, which describes this great turning point, the dawning of the reign of terror,
sentences.zh: 所以，这段描述了这一伟大转折点、恐怖统治曙光的文字，

sentences.en: comes from the single most influential history of the French Revolution that has ever been written in our native tongue.
sentences.zh: 出自我们母语中写就的、最具影响力的法国大革命历史著作。

sentences.en: And the man who wrote it was one of the absolute intellectual titans of Victorian Britain.
sentences.zh: 而写下它的人，正是维多利亚时代英国最顶尖的知识巨匠之一。

sentences.en: He was the Scottish historian and philosopher Thomas Carlyle.
sentences.zh: 他就是苏格兰历史学家兼哲学家托马斯·卡莱尔。

sentences.en: Now, some of you might have found that reading a little bit theatrical, but, of course, that was Carlyle's style.
sentences.zh: 现在，你们中的一些人可能会觉得这段朗读有点戏剧化，但当然，这就是卡莱尔的风格。

sentences.en: Some people might even say a melodramatic style, and I think they'd be right.
sentences.zh: 有些人甚至会说这是一种情节剧式的风格，我想他们说得对。

sentences.en: So, he's writing often the present tense, so it gives you this incredibly vivid, palpable sense of immediacy.
sentences.zh: 因此，他经常使用现在时写作，这带给你一种极其生动、感同身受的当场感。

sentences.en: He puts you right in the heart of the Revolution.
sentences.zh: 他把你直接带入了革命的核心。

sentences.en: And as you can tell from that passage, Tom, Carlyle sees the Revolution as the equivalent of the flood or the apocalypse in the Book of Revelation,
sentences.zh: 正如你从那段文字中所能感受到的，汤姆，卡莱尔将这场革命视为《启示录》中的洪水或天启的等同物，

sentences.en: this titanic biblical reckoning between the forces of radicalism and violence and the forces of the established order.
sentences.zh: 这是激进主义和暴力力量与建制秩序力量之间一场震撼人心的圣经式较量。

sentences.en: And the terror, this point in our story, 1793, 1794, is the absolute climax.
sentences.zh: 而恐怖统治——我们故事中的这个节点，即1793年、1794年——则是绝对的高潮。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, Carlyle casts it as this kind of immense, unstoppable conflagration that consumes all in its path and even its own profits.
sentences.zh: 因此，卡莱尔将其描绘成一种巨大而势不可挡的大火，吞噬着它道路上的一切，甚至是它自己的弄潮儿。

sentences.en: So, Saturn devouring its own children.
sentences.zh: 也就是萨图恩吞噬自己的孩子。

sentences.en: We talked about that in our first episode.
sentences.zh: 我们在第一集中讨论过这一点。

sentences.en: And also, Dominic, in our first episode, we talked about how for the British and perhaps for the Anglophone world more generally,
sentences.zh: 而且，多米尼克，在我们的第一集中，我们还讨论了对于英国人、或者也许对于更广泛的英语世界来说，

sentences.en: the terror is really what the Revolution is all about.
sentences.zh: 恐怖统治实际上才是这场革命的核心所在。

sentences.en: And it's not a coincidence that Carlyle was a massive influence on Charles Dickens, who said that he'd read it 500 times, Carlyle's book on the French Revolution.
sentences.zh: 卡莱尔对查尔斯·狄更斯产生了巨大的影响，这并非巧合，狄更斯曾说他读过卡莱尔的《法国大革命》500遍。

sentences.en: And so, it's his principal source for Tale of Two Cities, which is, I mean, amazing, the bestselling novel in English.
sentences.zh: 因此，这是他创作《双城记》的主要素材，我的意思是，这太惊人了，这是英语世界最畅销的小说。

sentences.en: So, that is the novel that's imprinted, this idea of the revolution as being equivalent to terror, I think, in the kind of the British imagination.
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为正是这部小说在英国人的想象中烙下了这种印象，即将革命等同于恐怖。

sentences.en: And this is where our sense of it as streams of blood, tumbrils, all of that that we were talking about yesterday comes from.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们对它血流成河、运囚车等所有昨天讨论过的事物的印象的来源。

sentences.en: And I would say that in Britain, far more than any other European country, the terror is actually seen almost as synonymous with the French Revolution itself.
sentences.zh: 我要说的是，在英国，恐怖统治受到的关注远远超过任何其他欧洲国家，它甚至几乎被视为法国大革命本身的同义词。

sentences.en: Completely.
sentences.zh: 完全如此。

sentences.en: So, actually, in a lot of European countries, there is an emphasis on the kind of the more progressive elements of the revolution.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在许多欧洲国家，人们更强调革命中较为进步的成分。

sentences.en: The metric system.
sentences.zh: 比如公制系统。

sentences.en: Not just the metric system, but the language of rights and that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是公制系统，还有权利的语言诸如此类。

sentences.en: But by and large, for the British, it's just mad people chopping each other's heads off.
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，对英国人而言，这就是一群疯子在互相砍头。

sentences.en: And do you know the person who magnificently, magnificently summed this up?
sentences.zh: 你知道是谁精妙绝伦地总结了这一点吗？

sentences.en: I do.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: I know what you're going to say.
sentences.zh: 我知道你要说什么。

sentences.en: So, this is an interview that Madame Satur gave in 1989 to Le Monde.
sentences.zh: 这是撒切尔夫人1989年接受《世界报》采访时说的一段话。

sentences.en: 1989, of course, is the bicentennial of Bastille Day, the start of the French Revolution.
sentences.zh: 当然，1989年是巴士底日（法国大革命的开端）两百周年纪念。

sentences.en: And it was part of a series of interviews with leaders from the G7 who were attending a summit in Paris.
sentences.zh: 这是对出席巴黎峰会的七国集团领导人系列采访的一部分。

sentences.en: And all the other six leaders were incredibly respectful of the revolution and everything that it had given humanity.
sentences.zh: 其他六位领导人都对革命及其赋予人类的一切表现得极其尊崇。

sentences.en: So, all this language of rights and stuff.
sentences.zh: 也就是所有关于权利之类的话语。

sentences.en: Mrs. Thatcher, absolutely uncompromising refusal to be diplomatic.
sentences.zh: 撒切尔夫人则表现出绝对毫不妥协、拒绝外交辞令的态度。

sentences.en: And she said that the revolution was a terrible thing.
sentences.zh: 她说这场革命是一件可怕的事情。

sentences.en: Up to the final death of Robespierre.
sentences.zh: 一直到罗伯斯庇尔最终死去。

sentences.en: Oh, it was an age of terror.
sentences.zh: 哦，那是一个恐怖的时代。

sentences.en: It was an age of terror.
sentences.zh: 那是一个恐怖的时代。

sentences.en: We did ours much more quietly.
sentences.zh: 我们（的革命）要平和得多。

sentences.en: She's not entirely wrong, to be fair.
sentences.zh: 平心而论，她并不完全算错。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, I suppose we did chop off the head of a king, but I think she's talking about the glorious revolution.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，我想我们确实砍掉了一个国王的头，但我想她指的是光荣革命。

sentences.en: And, you know, there was a lack of guillotining in that.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，那里面缺乏断头台。

sentences.en: And so, you said that in this series, we're going to be looking at the reality behind the myth.
sentences.zh: 所以，你曾说过在本系列中我们将探讨神话背后的现实。

sentences.en: And for British listeners, the myth is this notion of the revolution being all about terror.
sentences.zh: 对于英国听众来说，这个神话就是关于革命完全等同于恐怖的观念。

sentences.en: And so, listeners may be thinking, this idea of terror, is this just a kind of francophobic, British, something that they've imagined, something perhaps made up by Carlyle,
sentences.zh: 因此，听众可能会想，这种恐怖的观念，这只是一种恐法症、英国人想象出来的东西，也许是卡莱尔捏造出来的东西，

sentences.en: one of his rhetorical flourishes, one of his melodramatic flourishes.
sentences.zh: 是他那些修辞手法之一，是他那些情节剧式的修辞花招之一。

sentences.en: But actually, it's not at all.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，根本不是这样的。

sentences.en: Because the idea of terror being the order of the day, it originates with the revolutionaries themselves, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 因为“恐怖是当务之急”这个观念，最初正是由革命者自己提出的，不是吗？

sentences.en: Completely, it does.
sentences.zh: 完全是这样的。

sentences.en: They never use the phrase, they don't call themselves terrorists, as some historians later do.
sentences.zh: 他们从未真正使用过这个短语，他们不像后来的某些历史学家那样称自己为恐怖分子。

sentences.en: Nor do they ever use the expression, the reign of terror, as lots of historians do, and it's very common in the popular imagination.
sentences.zh: 他们也从未使用过“恐怖统治”这个词，尽管许多历史学家这样用，而且这在公众想象中非常普遍。

sentences.en: But the word terror, and terror as a positive political policy, as a strategy, as a deliberate choice, is there from 1793.
sentences.zh: 但是“恐怖”这个词，以及将恐怖作为一项积极的政治政策、一种战略、一种刻意的选择，从1793年起就已经存在了。

sentences.en: And arguably, even earlier, is implicit in a lot of what they're saying, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 甚至可以说更早，在他们很多言论中就已经暗含了这一点，不是吗？

sentences.en: So, that phrase that Carlyle quotes, let terror be the order of the day, he is quoting a slogan that was publicly pronounced by a man called Bertrand Barrère,
sentences.zh: 所以，卡莱尔引用的那句名言“让恐怖成为当务之急”，他引用的是一个由贝特朗·巴雷尔公开宣称的口号，

sentences.en: who was one of the 12 men who sat on the Committee of Public Safety, which we talked about yesterday,
sentences.zh: 巴雷尔是昨天我们谈到的公共安全委员会的12名成员之一，

sentences.en: this kind of proto-dictatorial institution that had been set up on the 6th of April, 1793.
sentences.zh: 这是一个在1793年4月6日建立的准独裁机构。

sentences.en: And it was never enshrined as a kind of official policy.
sentences.zh: 它从未被确立为一种官方政策。

sentences.en: It was never an official motion of the National Convention, which in effect was the government of revolutionary France, but it didn't need to be adopted as an official policy.
sentences.zh: 它从未成为国民公会（实际上是法国革命政府）的官方动议，但它不需要被采纳为官方政策。

sentences.en: And Barrère proclaimed it on the 5th of September, 1793, so some two months after the murder of Marat, which we were talking about in the previous episode.
sentences.zh: 巴雷尔在1793年9月5日宣布了这一点，也就是我们在上一集中谈到的马拉被刺杀大约两个月后。

sentences.en: And Barrère was offering this policy of terror as a way of dealing with all the multiple interlocking crises that we heard about in that first episode.
sentences.zh: 巴雷尔提出这项恐怖政策，是为了应对我们在第一集中听到的那些多重交织的危机。

sentences.en: So, war, counter-revolution, civil war, economic collapse, the collapse of the revolutionaries themselves into kind of bloodthirsty faction fighting.
sentences.zh: 也就是战争、反革命、内战、经济崩溃，以及革命者自身陷入嗜血派系斗争的崩溃。

sentences.en: And Barrère's goal in saying, let terror be the order of the day, was to institutionalise repression against the perceived enemies of the revolution and thereby to save it.
sentences.zh: 巴雷尔提出“让恐怖成为当务之急”的目标，是将对革命潜在敌人的镇压制度化，从而拯救革命。

sentences.en: And what this meant in practice was to reframe what had hitherto been ad hoc violence, violence that kind of emerged from the streets.
sentences.zh: 这在实践中意味着，将迄今为止那些临时拼凑的、从街头涌现的暴力进行重新定义。

sentences.en: Yeah, the September massacres in the prisons, for example.
sentences.zh: 是的，例如监狱中的九月大屠杀。

sentences.en: Chaotic, anarchic.
sentences.zh: 混乱的，无政府状态的。

sentences.en: All of that.
sentences.zh: 所有这些。

sentences.en: And to reframe it as a kind of formal state policy.
sentences.zh: 并将其重新构建为一种正式的国家政策。

sentences.en: But just to reiterate, even this is, it's still fundamentally an attempt at crisis management.
sentences.zh: 但需要重申的是，即便如此，这本质上仍然是一种危机管理的尝试。

sentences.en: It's an emergency measure.
sentences.zh: 这是一项应急措施。

sentences.en: It's a response to the crisis that is overwhelming the revolution.
sentences.zh: 这是对压垮革命的危机的回应。

sentences.en: It strikes me that there's two different schools of thought here, two different kinds of terror.
sentences.zh: 这让我觉得这里存在两种不同的思想流派，两种不同形式的恐怖。

sentences.en: So, what you're describing as the crisis management is terror as defensive.
sentences.zh: 所以，你所描述的危机管理是防御性的恐怖。

sentences.en: It's terror as in, you know, this is a bulwark against our enemies.
sentences.zh: 恐怖意味着，你知道，这是抵御我们敌人的堡垒。

sentences.en: But there is another way of thinking about the terror, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 但还有另一种思考恐怖的方式，不是吗？

sentences.en: Which is much more almost terror as a positive force.
sentences.zh: 那几乎更接近于将恐怖视为一种积极的力量。

sentences.en: Terror on the offensive.
sentences.zh: 进攻性的恐怖。

sentences.en: Terror as remodelling society or giving you a kind of, I suppose, a philosophy of government.
sentences.zh: 将恐怖视为重塑社会的方式，或者给你提供一种，我想，某种政府哲学。

sentences.en: And this brings us to the person at the heart of the story.
sentences.zh: 这就把我们带到了故事核心的人物身上。

sentences.en: I mean, you might say literally a bloodbath, that the blood washes away the taints of monarchy and aristocracy and superstition.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你甚至可以说是血洗，鲜血洗去了君主制、贵族制和迷信的污点。

sentences.en: And that you have to have the bloodbath so that something purer and better can emerge from it.
sentences.zh: 你必须经历血洗，这样更纯洁、更美好的东西才能从中诞生。

sentences.en: And this is quite a minority position in the beginning of 1793, but it will become increasingly influential.
sentences.zh: 在1793年初，这还是一个相当少数派的立场，但它将变得越来越具有影响力。

sentences.en: And the person who is most associated with it, probably the most famous or maybe notorious figure in the whole French Revolution,
sentences.zh: 与它联系最紧密的人，可能是整个法国大革命中最著名或也许是声名狼藉的人物，

sentences.en: was the one revolutionary that was name-checked by Mrs. Thatcher in that interview with Le Monde.
sentences.zh: 正是撒切尔夫人在接受《世界报》采访时点名提到的那个革命者。

sentences.en: And who, on the 5th of September, when Barrère proclaimed terror, the order of the day, was actually the president of the convention.
sentences.zh: 在9月5日巴雷尔宣称“恐怖是当务之急”时，他实际上正是国民公会的主席。

sentences.en: And that is Maximilien Robespierre.
sentences.zh: 他就是马克西米连·罗伯斯庇尔。
zh_words: 马克西米连·罗伯斯庇尔

sentences.en: So, he is, people can probably have a sense of what he looks like.
sentences.zh: 所以，人们大概能想象出他长什么样。

sentences.en: He is, in 1793, 35 years old.
He is short.
sentences.zh: 他个子不高。

sentences.en: He is slender.
sentences.zh: 他很苗条。

sentences.en: He is pale.
sentences.zh: 他脸色苍白。

sentences.en: In his appearance, he's compared by one contemporary to a cat.
sentences.zh: 在容貌上，一位同时代的人把他比作一只猫。

sentences.en: That at some time, he looks like a kind of domestic tabby.
sentences.zh: 有时他看起来像一只家养的花猫。

sentences.en: At other times, like a fierce tiger.
sentences.zh: 有时又像一只凶猛的老虎。

sentences.en: In our previous series about the French Revolution, Robespierre has been kind of threaded through it.
sentences.zh: 在我们之前关于法国大革命的系列节目中，罗伯斯庇尔的身影一直贯穿其中。

sentences.en: You know, he's bobbed up from time to time and then gone away again.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他时而露面，时而隐去。

sentences.en: And he's not really, at that point, the undisputed star of the revolution.
sentences.zh: 在那个时候，他其实并不是无可争议的革命之星。

sentences.en: But this is the moment, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但这就是那个时刻，不是吗？

sentences.en: The sort of second half of 1793, when he finds himself cast or casts himself as the absolute central figure in the drama.
sentences.zh: 在1793年的下半年左右，他发现自己被推上或主动成为这场大戏的绝对核心人物。

sentences.en: And he becomes identified with the whole policy of terror.
sentences.zh: 他与整个恐怖政策划上了等号。

sentences.en: He embodies it.
sentences.zh: 他具象化了它。

sentences.en: He personifies it, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 他将其实体化了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Perceived as its architect.
sentences.zh: 被视为它的设计师。

sentences.en: Perhaps not always fairly, I would say, actually.
sentences.zh: 其实，也许这并不总是那么公平。

sentences.en: But he certainly articulates it more fluently and confidently than anybody else.
sentences.zh: 但他确实比任何人都更流利、更自信地阐述了它。

sentences.en: Yeah, so he becomes the face of the terror, both when it is being prosecuted and in the wake of it.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以无论是在恐怖政策推行期间还是在其消逝之后，他都成为了恐怖的化身。

sentences.en: And I mean, on the one hand, I mean, fewer people die in the terror than are killed in the British army on the first day of the Somme.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，一方面，在恐怖统治中死去的人数，甚至比索姆河战役第一天阵亡的英国士兵还要少。

sentences.en: I mean, that is one way of looking at it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是看待问题的一个角度。

sentences.en: On the other hand, I mean, a lot of people are killed in the terror.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，我的意思是，确实有很多人在恐怖统治中丧生。

sentences.en: So, something like 17,000 people across the whole of France get to be executed as traitors and enemies of the revolution.
sentences.zh: 因此，全法国大约有17000人作为叛徒和革命敌人被处决。

sentences.en: And then you were talking yesterday about the Vendée.
sentences.zh: 然后你昨天谈到了旺代。

sentences.en: I mean, a huge scale of slaughter there.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那里的屠杀规模极其庞大。

sentences.en: Some French historians compare it to genocide.
sentences.zh: 一些法国历史学家将其比作种族灭绝。

sentences.en: And certainly, in Paris, the centre of the revolution, there is a kind of hideous melodrama to the displays of executions that are going on.
sentences.zh: 当然，在革命的中心巴黎，正在进行的处决场面具有一种可怕的情节剧色彩。

sentences.en: I mean, this is why the guillotining is so memorable.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是断头台如此令人难忘的原因。

sentences.en: The guillotine was designed to be merciful, to be an enlightened way of killing people.
sentences.zh: 断头台的设计初衷是仁慈的，是一种开明的杀人方式。

sentences.en: But the speed with which the blade drops onto the neck results in great geysers of blood welling out.
sentences.zh: 但刀刃落入脖子的速度极快，导致大量鲜血喷涌而出。

sentences.en: So, it is a really spectacular, terrifying sight.
sentences.zh: 所以，这真的是一个极为壮观、令人毛骨悚然的景象。

sentences.en: And so much blood ends up flowing over the course of the terror into the water supply that it becomes poisoned.
sentences.zh: 在恐怖统治期间，最终流入供水系统的血量如此之多，以至于水源都被污染了。

sentences.en: And they have to move the guillotine because the blood is getting into the water system.
sentences.zh: 他们不得不移走断头台，因为鲜血已经渗入了供水系统。

sentences.en: And I think to his enemies, Robespierre comes to seem the embodiment of everything that is making this happen.
sentences.zh: 我想在政敌眼中，罗伯斯庇尔成了造成这一切的罪魁祸首的化身。

sentences.en: A kind of a monster who is threatening to turn the whole of France into a cemetery.
sentences.zh: 一个威胁要把整个法国变成墓地的恶魔。

sentences.en: And there is a famous cartoon which was published towards the end of the terror, which illustrates this.
sentences.zh: 在恐怖统治接近尾声时，曾发表过一幅著名的漫画，生动地说明了这一点。

sentences.en: And it shows Robespierre, to quote the caption, guillotining the executioner after having had all the French guillotined.
sentences.zh: 画面显示，用图说的话来说，罗伯斯庇尔在把所有法国人都送上断头台后，又把刽子手也送上了断头台。

sentences.en: So, this sense of the terror as something that will end up consuming the entire country.
sentences.zh: 因此，这就传达出一种感觉，即恐怖统治最终将吞噬整个国家。

sentences.en: And you mentioned the word terroriSt.
sentences.zh: 你提到了“恐怖分子”这个词。

sentences.en: So, it's originally coined in French in 1794, after the terror has formally been brought to an end, to describe a class of person who had never before needed to be described.
sentences.zh: 所以它最初是在1794年法国大革命恐怖时期正式结束之后在法语中创造的，用来描述一种以前从未需要被描述的一类人。

sentences.en: So, this is the birth of our notion of terrorism as a positive, because terrorists obviously think that they are doing often God's work or the work of the people or whatever.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们对恐怖主义作为一种积极事物的观念的诞生，因为恐怖分子显然认为他们通常是在替天行道或为人民服务之类的事情。

sentences.en: They do indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: But you know, you were talking about Robespierre.
sentences.zh: 但你知道，你刚才谈到了罗伯斯庇尔。

sentences.en: This idea that people have of Robespierre is this monster hungry for blood.
sentences.zh: 人们对罗伯斯庇尔的这种看法，认为他是一个渴望鲜血的恶魔。

sentences.en: I mean, it's so common.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这太普遍了。

sentences.en: It's common in political rhetoric.
sentences.zh: 这在政治修辞中很常见。

sentences.en: And Robespierre's bloodlust, his desire to sacrifice human life in pursuit of a better world, has become an absolute staple of conservative political thought, hasn't it, really?
sentences.zh: 罗伯斯庇尔对鲜血的渴望，他为了追求更美好的世界而牺牲人类生命的欲望，真的已经成为保守派政治思想的绝对核心主张了，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, he's a sort of monster haunting the conservative imagination.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他是萦绕在保守派想象中的某种恶魔。

sentences.en: And yet, the funny thing about Robespierre is when you look at him, in so many ways, you know, he is not Stalin or he's not Pol Pot or something.
sentences.zh: 然而，关于罗伯斯庇尔有趣的地方在于，当你审视他时，在许多方面，你知道，他并不是斯大林，也不是波尔布特之流。

sentences.en: So, you give the example, don't you, in your notes.
sentences.zh: 所以你在笔记里举了例子，不是吗？

sentences.en: But at a really obvious point, Robespierre is personally extremely squeamish.
sentences.zh: 但在一个显而易见的问题上，罗伯斯庇尔在个人方面极其胆小、见血发晕。

sentences.en: And this will astound people.
sentences.zh: 这会让人大吃一惊。

sentences.en: This man who is famous for guillotining all these thousands of people, he, all his life, had consistently opposed capital punishment.
sentences.zh: 这个因将成千上万的人送上断头台而闻名的人，他一生中其实一直坚决反对死刑。

sentences.en: Completely.
sentences.zh: 完全是这样。

sentences.en: We did an episode on the introduction of the guillotine and how Robespierre stood up right the way through all the meetings that were structuring the revolution from 1789 onwards,
sentences.zh: 我们曾做过一集关于断头台引入的节目，讲述了罗伯斯庇尔如何从1789年开始一直坚定地出席所有筹划革命的会议，

sentences.en: opposing the death penalty.
sentences.zh: 反对死刑。

sentences.en: And he had a profound personal horror of violence.
sentences.zh: 他内心对暴力有着极深的恐惧。

sentences.en: For instance, he had opposed the war against Austria and Prussia that the Girondins had pushed.
sentences.zh: 例如，他曾反对吉伦特派极力推行的对奥地利和普鲁士的战争。

sentences.en: He was very against it.
sentences.zh: 他非常反对。

sentences.en: Even though, ultimately, he is part of the institution that is responsible for sending people to the guillotine, he never goes and watches executions himself.
sentences.zh: 尽管他最终属于那个将人们送上断头台的机构，但他自己从不去观看行刑。

sentences.en: He hasn't got the stomach for it.
sentences.zh: 他实在没有这个勇气。

sentences.en: And even during the terror itself, he does disapprove of a lot of the more indiscriminate atrocities that are being perpetrated out in the provinces.
sentences.zh: 甚至在恐怖统治期间，他也确实不赞成在外省发生的大量无差别的暴行。

sentences.en: We talked yesterday about Marat, how the stress of being in the eye of the political storm brought him out in kind of boils and all kinds of skin complaints.
sentences.zh: 我们昨天谈到了马拉，谈到处于政治风暴眼中的压力如何让他的身体长出各种疖子和皮肤病。

sentences.en: I think Robespierre, likewise, finds the process of administering the terror very stressful, which I'm sure won't be much consolation to those who are his victiMs.
sentences.zh: 我想罗伯斯庇尔同样觉得管理恐怖统治的过程压力巨大，这对于他的受害者们来说肯定算不上什么安慰。

sentences.en: But it is notable that he seems to have retired to his bed in a state of kind of nervous collapse throughout the months of the terror.
sentences.zh: 但值得注意的是，在恐怖统治的几个月里，他似乎一直处于神经崩溃的状态而卧床不起。

sentences.en: So, as you say, he's absolutely not Stalin.
sentences.zh: 所以，正如你所说，他绝对不是斯大林。

sentences.en: He's not cavalier about this.
sentences.zh: 他对此并非漫不经心。

sentences.en: He feels the burden of it, I think, very personally.
sentences.zh: 我认为，他非常深刻地感受到了这种沉重的负担。

sentences.en: And also, his political opinions.
sentences.zh: 还有他的政治观点。

sentences.en: I mean, they are very liberal Democrat.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它们是非常自由主义民主的。

sentences.en: They're very inoffensive.
sentences.zh: 它们非常无害。

sentences.en: They are exactly the kind of thing that today constitutes the political mainstream for parties in pretty much every Western democracy, I would say.
sentences.zh: 我想，这恰恰是当今几乎所有西方民主国家政党所代表的政治主流。

sentences.en: We mentioned how Robespierre opposes the death penalty.
sentences.zh: 我们提到了罗伯斯庇尔是如何反对死刑的。

sentences.en: He also is a keen supporter of freedom of the press.
sentences.zh: 他也是新闻自由的坚定支持者。

sentences.en: He's backed this throughout his life.
sentences.zh: 他一生都在支持这一点。

sentences.en: He's in favour of universal male suffrage, not female suffrage, although he is incredibly popular with revolutionary women, as we will see.
sentences.zh: 他赞成成年男子普选权，而不是妇女普选权，尽管正如我们将看到的，他极其受革命女性的欢迎。

sentences.en: He supports progressive taxation to support universal education.
sentences.zh: 他支持通过累进税制来支持全民教育。

sentences.en: He supports the idea of human rights.
sentences.zh: 他支持人权的理念。

sentences.en: He's a firm believer in them.
sentences.zh: 他是人权的坚定信仰者。

sentences.en: And he's an abolitioniSt.
sentences.zh: 他是一名废奴主义者。

sentences.en: He wants to see slavery go.
sentences.zh: 他希望看到奴隶制消失。

sentences.en: So, these are all pretty politically impeccable positions from the perspective of today.
sentences.zh: 因此，从今天的角度来看，这些在政治上都是无可挑剔的立场。

sentences.en: Woke God in reading Snowflake.
sentences.zh: 真是个与时俱进的温和派。

sentences.en: Who knew?
sentences.zh: 谁能想到呢？

sentences.en: A further thing that is strange about him.
sentences.zh: 关于他的另一个奇怪之处。

sentences.en: We were talking yesterday about how Marat dresses in a way that makes him seem the embodiment of the revolution.
sentences.zh: 我们昨天谈到马拉的着装方式如何让他看起来像是革命的化身。

sentences.en: He dresses as a child of the street and how by 1793, this is something that most revolutionaries are doing.
sentences.zh: 他穿得像个街头之子，到了1793年，大多数革命者都在这么做。

sentences.en: This is not Robespierre's vibe at all.
sentences.zh: 这可完全不是罗伯斯庇尔的风格。

sentences.en: Robespierre's vibe does not remotely seem that of a revolutionary itching to drown the ancien regime in blood.
sentences.zh: 罗伯斯庇尔的风格一点也不像那种急于将旧制度淹没在血海中的革命者。

sentences.en: So, Timothy Tackett in his book on the terror, which we've been quoting a lot in this series, he quotes one of Robespierre's colleagues in 1793,
sentences.zh: 因此，蒂莫西·塔克特在他关于恐怖统治的书（我们在本系列中经常引用）中，引用了罗伯斯庇尔在1793年的一位同僚的话，

sentences.en: who is very into this notion of kind of repudiating aristocratic fashion.
sentences.zh: 这个人非常热衷于摒弃贵族时尚这种概念。

sentences.en: And this guy says, we now all look like beggars, boots and threadbare clothing, such is our stylish costume.
sentences.zh: 这个人说，我们现在看起来都像乞丐，穿着靴子和磨损的衣服，这就是我们时髦的行头。

sentences.en: These are the clothes that people in the convention are wearing almost as a kind of uniform.
sentences.zh: 国民公会里的成员穿的衣服几乎就像是一种制服。

sentences.en: But Robespierre, I mean, for him, it might as well be Versailles in 1781 or something.
sentences.zh: 但罗伯斯庇尔，我的意思是，对她而言，这跟1781年的凡尔赛没什么两样。

sentences.en: So, he loves a powdered wig.
sentences.zh: 所以，他极度喜爱带粉的假发。

sentences.en: He loves an embroidered waistcoat.
sentences.zh: 他极度喜爱刺绣背心。

sentences.en: He loves a waistcoat.
sentences.zh: 他非常喜欢背心。

sentences.en: Robespierre loves silk stockings.
sentences.zh: 罗伯斯庇尔喜欢丝袜。

sentences.en: He loves a handsome blue coat.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢一件漂亮的蓝色外套。

sentences.en: And the thing about the stockings is interesting because, of course, the culotte are the britches that the aristocracy used to wear at Versailles to complement the stockings.
sentences.zh: 关于丝袜的事很有趣，因为当然，阔腿裤就是贵族以前在凡尔赛穿着来搭配丝袜的马裤。

sentences.en: And so, the sans-culotte is people who wear trousers, people who can't afford this style.
sentences.zh: 因此，“无套裤汉”就是指穿长裤的人，指那些买不起这种款式的人。

sentences.en: And as early as 1791, Robespierre had been described by a fellow revolutionary as the general of the sans-culotte.
sentences.zh: 早在1791年，罗伯斯庇尔就被一位革命同僚称为“无套裤汉的将军”。

sentences.en: But Robespierre himself, despite being the general of the sans-culotte, he's still wearing culotte.
sentences.zh: 但罗伯斯庇尔自己，尽管是无套裤汉的将军，却依然穿着马裤。

sentences.en: He has them.
sentences.zh: 他拥有它们。

sentences.en: He's wearing his pantaloons.
sentences.zh: 他穿着他的裤子。

sentences.en: And so, it is striking that the man who, more than anyone else, is associated with sweeping away the old order should affect the fashions of that very order.
sentences.zh: 因此，令人震惊的是，这个比任何人都更与扫除旧秩序联系在一起的人，竟然还在模仿旧秩序的时尚。

sentences.en: Yeah, because he's so prim.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为他太古板了。

sentences.en: He's so meticulous.
sentences.zh: 他太一丝不苟了。

sentences.en: He's so dapper.
sentences.zh: 他太讲究了。

sentences.en: Fastidious.
sentences.zh: 极其挑剔。

sentences.en: Now, what's going on there?
sentences.zh: 那么，这到底是是怎么回事？

sentences.en: How do you reconcile those two things?
sentences.zh: 你如何将这两件事调和起来？

sentences.en: I mean, it's fascinating from the point of view of personal psychology.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，从个人心理学的角度来看，这非常迷人。

sentences.en: But I think it also matters because looking at Robespierre's character and background helps us as well maybe to get a handle on what's going on in the terror because Robespierre is so influential on it.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这也十分重要，因为审视罗伯斯庇尔的性格和背景，也有助于我们或许能理解恐怖统治期间发生了什么，因为罗伯斯庇尔对它的影响太大了。

sentences.en: And so, before we carry the story on from the death of Marat, all the turbulent events that we'll be following that,
sentences.zh: 因此，在我们从马拉之死以及随之而来的所有动荡事件继续推进故事之前，

sentences.en: let's just have a quick look at Robespierre's backstory because we haven't given it yet in the course of our various series on the French Revolution.
sentences.zh: 让我们简单回顾一下罗伯斯庇尔的背景故事，因为在我们关于法国大革命的各个系列中，我们还没有讲过它。

sentences.en: Maybe see what clues we can find there.
sentences.zh: 也许能看看我们在那里能找到什么线索。

sentences.en: Love a clue.
sentences.zh: 最喜欢找线索了。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: So, Robespierre was born on the 6th of May, 1758 in Arras, which is a town on France's borders with Holland.
sentences.zh: 所以，罗伯斯庇尔于1758年5月6日出生在阿拉斯，这是法国与荷兰边境的一个城镇。

sentences.en: And it's very prosperous, it's very pious, and it's unbelievably boring.
sentences.zh: 那里非常繁荣，非常笃信宗教，而且无聊得难以置信。

sentences.en: And Robespierre's early life is marked by kind of repeated tragedies and petty humiliations and reading about them kind of remind me of 19th century novels that always feature these kind of things,
sentences.zh: 罗伯斯庇尔的早年生活以一再的悲剧和平庸的屈辱为标志，读到这些让我有点想起19世纪的小说，总是以这些东西为特色，

sentences.en: Madame Bovary or something like that, where there are small scale tragedies, but obviously incredibly personally felt if you are the person experiencing them.
sentences.zh: 比如《包法利夫人》之类的小说，里面都是小规模的悲剧，但如果你是经历它们的人，显然会产生极其深刻的个人感受。

sentences.en: And do you remember how we were talking in the Marat episode about how Robert Darnton has this thing about so many of the revolutionaries have a sense of disappointment,
sentences.zh: 你还记得我们在马拉那一集里谈过罗伯特·达恩顿的观点吗？他说许多革命者在早年生活中都有失落感、挫折感（个人或职业上的），这让他们产生了一种怨恨和未竟的事业。

sentences.en: frustration, personal, professional, in their early lives that gives them a sense of resentment and unfinished business.
sentences.zh: 我想罗伯斯庇尔也是这样吗？

sentences.en: And I wonder if that's the case with Robespierre.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他绝对有一种，有什么东西在折磨他，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, he definitely has a, there's something gnawing at him, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 是的，所以在这种背景下，我的意思是，让我们看看他的父母。

sentences.en: Yeah, so in that context, I mean, let's look at his parents.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲是一名律师，非常不稳定，社会阶层大幅下滑。

sentences.en: So his father was a lawyer who was very unstable and very downwardly mobile.
sentences.zh: 他让罗伯斯庇尔的母亲怀孕了，而母亲是一位酿酒师未婚的女儿，所以阶层比律师低得多。

sentences.en: And he had got Robespierre's mother, who was the unmarried daughter of a brewer, so considerably lower class to a lawyer.
sentences.zh: 他让她怀孕了。

sentences.en: He got her pregnant.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一场奉子成婚，马克西米利安在他父母婚礼四个月后出生。

sentences.en: So it was a shotgun wedding and Maximilien was born four months after his parents' wedding.
sentences.zh: 他的父母接着又有了三个孩子。

sentences.en: And his parents go on to have three more children.
sentences.zh: 马克西米利安的弟弟奥古斯丁，以及两个妹妹夏洛特和亨丽埃特。

sentences.en: So a brother for Maximilien, Augustin, and two sisters, Charlotte and Henriette.
sentences.zh: 然后父亲的存在感越来越低。

sentences.en: And then father is an increasingly absent presence.
sentences.zh: 他的直线坠落仍在继续。

sentences.en: His downward spiral continues.
sentences.zh: 他们的母亲一直都在，所有的孩子显然都非常崇拜她。

sentences.en: Their mother is a continuous presence and all her children clearly adored her.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，当1764年马克西米利安只有六岁时她去世时，这种冲击对所有四个孩子来说，我认为都是一个彻底粉碎性的打击。

sentences.en: And so that means that when in 1764, when Maximilien was only six, she dies, the impact is felt, I think, by all four children as a completely crushing blow.
sentences.zh: 马克西米利安尤其是深受打击。

sentences.en: And Maximilien in particular was devastated.
sentences.zh: 在他的成年生活中，每当提到他的母亲，他都会热泪盈眶。

sentences.en: And throughout his adult life, whenever his mother was mentioned, tears would come to his eyes.
sentences.zh: 他会彻底哭出来。

sentences.en: He would completely tear up.
sentences.zh: 他们的父亲基本上已经消失了。

sentences.en: Their father basically by now has vanished.
sentences.zh: 他不是那种准备好承担照顾四个失去母亲的孩子的负担的人。

sentences.en: He is not the kind of man who is prepared to shoulder the burden of looking after four motherless children.
sentences.zh: 他从现场消失了。

sentences.en: He vanishes from the scene.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些孩子最终被分配给各种亲戚照顾。

sentences.en: And so the children end up being divided up between kind of various relatives.
sentences.zh: 两个女孩去和她们的姑姑们一起住。

sentences.en: So the two girls go to live with their paternal aunts.
sentences.zh: 两个男孩，马克西米利安和奥古斯丁，去和他们的祖父母（也就是酿酒师）一起住。

sentences.en: And the two boys, Maximilien and Augustin, go to live with their paternal grandparents, who are the brewers.
sentences.zh: 彼得·麦克菲在其极佳的罗伯斯庇尔传记中写道，尽管马克西米利安出生于一个律师和官员的长寿家族，

sentences.en: And Peter McPhee, in his biography of Ross-Pierre, brilliant biography, writes that although born into a long line of lawyers and officials,
sentences.zh: 但现在他要在鲁·龙维尔街的马车声和当地皮卡第方言的工人们叫喊的手工劳动环境中长大。

sentences.en: Maximilien was now to be brought up in a milieu of manual work with the sounds of carts and workers shouting in the local Picard dialect in the Rue Ronville.
sentences.zh: 所以，一方面，这或许给了他一种对工人的认同感，对那些用双手劳动的人的认同感。

sentences.en: So, on the one hand, perhaps this is giving him a sense of identification with the workers, people who are working with their hands.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，你可以理解为什么他可能想要紧紧抓住体面的外在标志。

sentences.en: On the other hand, you can understand why he would perhaps have wanted to hold on to the outward signs of respectability.
sentences.zh: 因此就有了这些衣服。

sentences.en: Hence the clothes.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为那里有一种耐人寻味的张力。

sentences.en: So I think there is a kind of intriguing tension there.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 而且这绝对在他身上产生了一种不安全感，正如他在母亲去世同年（也就是他六岁时）的遭遇一样，

sentences.en: And definitely it generates a sense of insecurity in him, as also does the fact that the same year that his mother dies, so when he's six,
sentences.zh: 他得了天花，脸上留下了麻子。

sentences.en: he gets smallpox and it leaves his face kind of pockmarked.
sentences.zh: 所以他可能有点边缘化。

sentences.en: So he's a little bit marginal, maybe.
sentences.zh: 感觉有点像个局外人。

sentences.en: It feels a bit out of an outsider.
sentences.zh: 他不太合群。

sentences.en: He doesn't quite fit.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他和酿酒师们格格不入。

sentences.en: You know, he doesn't fit with the brewers.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 但同样，他在酿酒师家庭长大的事实，意味着他与他渴望加入的中产阶级也有些格格不入。

sentences.en: But equally, the fact that he's been brought up by brewers means he doesn't quite fit with the middle class people that he aspires to join.
sentences.zh: 另一件事，当然，他不是个爱玩的人，对吧？

sentences.en: And the other thing, of course, he's not a funster, is he?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想毫不奇怪，当你想到这一点时，你知道，所有他经历过的悲剧，他根本不是个爱玩的人。

sentences.en: Well, I think unsurprisingly, when you think of that, you know, all the kind of tragedies he's been through, he's not a funster.
sentences.zh: 他成长为一个非常严肃、焦虑、内向的小男孩。

sentences.en: He grows up a very earnest, anxious, reserved little boy.
sentences.zh: 他绝对不是生活中那种热衷于聚会的人。

sentences.en: And he's definitely not one of life's party animals.
sentences.zh: 所以他的妹妹夏洛特多年后在写到他的童年时回忆说，他极少玩游戏，而当他参与游戏时，他的角色，

sentences.en: So his sister, Charlotte, years later, writing about his childhood, recalled that he very rarely played games and that when he was involved in the games, his role,
sentences.zh: 他最热衷的核心事情就是澄清和坚持规则。

sentences.en: the chief thing that he was into was clarifying and insisting on the rules.
sentences.zh: 噢，不，最糟糕的那种小孩。

sentences.en: Oh, no, the worst kind of child.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以，同样地，这其中是否包含了他日后为自己确立的角色的线索？

sentences.en: So, again, whether there is a clue there as to the role that he will adopt for himself in due course.
sentences.zh: 他也，我很喜欢他这一点，他是个鸽子迷。

sentences.en: He's also, and I like this about him, he's a great fan of the pigeon.
sentences.zh: 所以，就像戈登·卡雷拉和我自己一样，喜欢鸽子和麻雀。

sentences.en: So, like Gordon Carrera and myself, pigeons and sparrows.
sentences.zh: 他饲养它们、喂养它们并且照顾它们。

sentences.en: And he keeps them and feeds them and kind of looks after them.
sentences.zh: 他的妹妹们总是恳求他允许她们照顾这些鸽子。

sentences.en: And his sisters were always begging him to be allowed to look after these pigeons.
sentences.zh: 马克西米利安非常不情愿，因为他不信任她们。

sentences.en: And Maximilian was very reluctant because he didn't trust them.
sentences.zh: 最后他妥协了，而女孩们不可避免地把罗伯斯庇尔最喜欢的鸽子留在了花园外面。

sentences.en: And finally, he gives in and the girls inevitably leave Robespierre's favourite pigeon outside in the garden.
sentences.zh: 结果遇到了一场暴风雨，鸽子死了。

sentences.en: There's a storm and the pigeon dies.
sentences.zh: 夏洛特回忆说，听到这个死讯时，马克西米利安的眼泪夺眶而出。

sentences.en: And Charlotte recalled how at the news of this death, the tears of Maximilian flowed.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切眼泪，这就是情感的时代。

sentences.en: So all these tears, this is the age of sentiment.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 一只鸽子的死。

sentences.en: Death of a pigeon.
sentences.zh: 罗伯斯庇尔完全沉浸在那样的感伤之中。

sentences.en: Robespierre is totally buying into that kind of sensibility.
sentences.zh: 鸽子怎么会在暴风雨中死掉呢？

sentences.en: Why would the pigeon die in a storm?
sentences.zh: 这就是让我费解的地方。

sentences.en: That's what baffles me.
sentences.zh: 鸽子通常不会在暴风雨中死掉。

sentences.en: Pigeons don't generally die in storMs.
sentences.zh: 我想可能是被闪电击中了。

sentences.en: Probably struck by lightning, I imagine.
sentences.zh: 被闪电击中？

sentences.en: Struck by lightning?
sentences.zh: 我只是提出一种假设。

sentences.en: I'm offering a thesis there.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我认为历史对此保持沉默。

sentences.en: I think history is silent on that.
sentences.zh: 所以他有麻子。

sentences.en: So he's potmarked.
sentences.zh: 他失去了母亲。

sentences.en: He's lost his mother.
sentences.zh: 他非常严肃。

sentences.en: He's very earneSt.
sentences.zh: 他不玩游戏。

sentences.en: He doesn't play games.
sentences.zh: 他失去了他的鸽子。

sentences.en: He's lost his pigeons.
sentences.zh: 你可能会认为他的处境糟透了。

sentences.en: You might think things are looking terrible for him.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，没关系，因为他聪明绝顶。

sentences.en: But actually, it's okay because he is brilliantly intelligent.
sentences.zh: 事实证明他是一个绝对优秀的优等生。

sentences.en: He turns out to be an absolutely superb student.
sentences.zh: 他赢得了进入精英耶稣会基金会的奖学金。

sentences.en: And he wins a scholarship to an elite Jesuit foundation.
sentences.zh: 此时它实际上并非由耶稣会士运营，因为他们已被驱逐出法国。

sentences.en: It's not actually being run by the Jesuits at this point because they've been expelled from France.
sentences.zh: 但它仍然保持着强调教育的耶稣会精神。

sentences.en: But it still maintains that Jesuit ethos of emphasising education.
sentences.zh: 这是一所位于巴黎的名叫路易大帝中学的学校。

sentences.en: And this is a school called the Collège Louis-le-Grand in Paris.
sentences.zh: 这所学校以前的校友包括莫里哀和伏尔泰。

sentences.en: And previous alumni of this school had included Moliere and Voltaire.
sentences.zh: 这所学校以前的校友包括莫里哀和伏尔泰。

sentences.en: And also, intriguingly, the Marquis de Sade.
sentences.zh: 而且还有个有意思的人，萨德侯爵。

sentences.en: So he'd been there too.
sentences.zh: 所以他也去过那里。

sentences.en: And I looked this up and the list of alumni who followed in Robespierre's Wake is amazing.
sentences.zh: 我查了一下，追随罗伯斯庇尔脚步的校友名单简直惊人。

sentences.en: So Victor Hugo, Sartre, Roland Barthes, Jacques Chirac.
sentences.zh: 比如维克多·雨果、萨特、罗兰·巴特、雅克·希拉克。

sentences.en: Jacques Chirac, friend of the show.
sentences.zh: 雅克·希拉克，节目的老朋友。

sentences.en: A man who loves a quick shower.
sentences.zh: 一个热爱洗快澡的男人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Mr. Five Minutes or whatever it was called.
sentences.zh: “五分钟先生”还是叫别的什么来着。

sentences.en: I think it was three minutes, wasn't it?
sentences.zh: 我觉得是三分钟，对吧？

sentences.en: Shower included.
sentences.zh: 连洗澡时间在内。

sentences.en: Remember?
sentences.zh: 还记得吗？

sentences.en: Jacques Derrida.
sentences.zh: 雅克·德里达。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Thomas Pinkety.
sentences.zh: 托马斯·品克蒂。

sentences.en: So, I mean, absolute roll call of famous French writers and intellectuals.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一份法国著名作家和知识分子的绝对名人录。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And Jacques Chirac.
sentences.zh: 还有雅克·希拉克。

sentences.en: Very good.
sentences.zh: 很好。

sentences.en: And when he's at the – it's when he's at the school that this incredibly famous mythologised
sentences.zh: 就在他——正是在这所学校里，发生了这个极其著名、被严重神话的

sentences.en: moment happens, which so many people see as the absolute key to Robespierre's career and indeed to the course of the French Revolution.
sentences.zh: 时刻，许多人认为这是罗伯斯庇尔职业生涯的绝对关键，也是法国大革命进程的关键。

sentences.en: So this is when he meets the royal couple.
sentences.zh: 这就是他与皇室夫妇见面的时候。

sentences.en: Well, tell the story, Tom, and tell me if it really is the key.
sentences.zh: 好了，讲讲这个故事吧，汤姆，并告诉我这真的是关键吗？

sentences.en: So Louis XVI and Marie Antoinette have gone to Reims to be anointed with the holy oil and to be crowned.
sentences.zh: 路易十六和玛丽·安托瓦内特去了兰斯，接受圣油涂抹并加冕。

sentences.en: And they're returning from their coronation.
sentences.zh: 他们正在从加冕典礼返回。

sentences.en: And the boys of the college Louis Le Grand have been preparing, you know, what sounds an unbelievably dull reception with lots of verse declamation in Latin.
sentences.zh: 路易大帝学院的男生们一直在筹备一场听起来无聊得令人难以置信的欢迎仪式，有大量的拉丁语诗歌朗诵。

sentences.en: And Robespierre, as the prize student, has been entrusted with the task of giving them a ceremonial speech of welcome.
sentences.zh: 而作为优等生，罗伯斯庇尔被委以重任，负责发表仪式欢迎辞。

sentences.en: And he has to wait outside for the royal coach to arrive.
sentences.zh: 他必须在外面等着皇家马车到来。

sentences.en: And it's bucketing down with rain.
sentences.zh: 当时正下着倾盆大雨。

sentences.en: And he's kneeling, waiting for them to arrive.
sentences.zh: 他跪在地上，等待他们到达。

sentences.en: And the coach lumbers up.
sentences.zh: 马车轰隆隆地驶来。

sentences.en: And because it's raining, the royal couple don't get out of the coach.
sentences.zh: 由于下雨，皇室夫妇没有下车。

sentences.en: They just sit in the coach and kind of smile politely.
sentences.zh: 他们只是坐在马车里，礼貌地微笑着。

sentences.en: They listen to this bedrackled schoolboy give what I'm sure is very, very dull talk.
sentences.zh: 他们听着这个落汤鸡般的中学生发表我确信非常非常无聊的讲话。

sentences.en: And they – when it's delivered, they acknowledge the speech with kind of polite smiles.
sentences.zh: 讲完后，他们用礼貌的微笑对演讲表示认可。

sentences.en: And then, you know, they give a signal and the carriage clatters off.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道的，他们给了一个信号，马车就哒哒地开走了。

sentences.en: And that's the end of it.
sentences.zh: 事情就这样结束了。

sentences.en: Hold on.
sentences.zh: 等等。

sentences.en: So, the version that I read sometimes is they didn't look at him.
sentences.zh: 所以，我有时读到的版本是他们根本没看他一眼。

sentences.en: They don't care.
sentences.zh: 他们根本不在乎。

sentences.en: They splash him with mud and water.
sentences.zh: 他们溅了他一身泥水。

sentences.en: No, they behave as politely as they can, but they don't want to get wet.
sentences.zh: 不，他们表现得尽可能礼貌，但他们不想淋湿。

sentences.en: That's reasonable.
sentences.zh: 这很合理。

sentences.en: I don't think that's unreasonable.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这并不过分。

sentences.en: But you can see that those stories that, you know, he gets splashed with mud and everything.
sentences.zh: 但你能看出，那些关于他被溅满泥水之类的故事。

sentences.en: This is being used to explain his hostility to the monarchy and his desire to bring down the old regime and all.
sentences.zh: 这被用来解释他对君主制的敌意以及他推翻旧政权的渴望之类的。

sentences.en: I don't think this is true at all.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这完全不是真的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: I mean, I think it probably didn't help make him into a monarchist or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得这大概没帮他变成保皇派之类的人。

sentences.en: I think it explains what is inspiring him in the revolution, because there are much, much more formative influences, as we will see.
sentences.zh: 我认为这解释了他在革命中受到了什么启发，因为正如我们所见，还有很多很多更具塑造性的影响。

sentences.en: So, Robson does very well at school.
sentences.zh: 所以，罗伯斯庇尔在学校表现很好。

sentences.en: He qualifies as a lawyer, and he returns to his hometown, where he makes a name for himself as a friend of the poor.
sentences.zh: 他获得了律师资格，回到家乡，作为穷人的朋友而名声大噪。

sentences.en: He is always taking on the cases of people who can't afford legal representation.
sentences.zh: 他总是接手那些请不起法律辩护的人的案件。

sentences.en: And so, he makes a good name for himself.
sentences.zh: 因此，他赢得了好名声。

sentences.en: People see him as a virtuous, principled person, an admirable person.
sentences.zh: 人们视他为一个正直、有原则的人，一个令人钦佩的人。

sentences.en: But having said that, I mean, he seems destined for a life of the utmost provincial obscurity, except that Robson-Pierre himself, I think, is daring to dream.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，我的意思是，他似乎注定要过一种极其默默无闻的地方官僚生活，只不过罗伯斯庇尔本人，我认为，敢于梦想。

sentences.en: He's daring to dream of a better life and a better order for France.
sentences.zh: 他敢于梦想为法国带来更好的生活和更好的秩序。

sentences.en: And the reason for this is the very familiar one, that he's been reading a lot of books.
sentences.zh: 原因很简单，他读了很多书。

sentences.en: Oh, that was a bad sign.
sentences.zh: 哦，那是个不好的征兆。

sentences.en: But he's been reading very particular books, hasn't he?
sentences.zh: 但他读的都是非常特殊的书，对吧？

sentences.en: We had talked about Charlotte Corday, reading Plutarch and Cornet in the previous episode.
sentences.zh: 我们上一集讨论过夏洛特·科黛阅读普鲁塔克和高乃依。

sentences.en: Basically, everybody in the French Revolution has read the same books, and Robson-Pierre has read all of them.
sentences.zh: 基本上，法国大革命中的每个人都读过相同的书，而罗伯斯庇尔把它们都读了。

sentences.en: Yeah, so back in the 17th century, Thomas Hobbes said that he would ban the reading of histories
sentences.zh: 对，所以在17世纪，托马斯·霍布斯曾说他会禁止阅读历史书

sentences.en: by the Greeks and the Romans because it just fostered rebellion and revolution against kings.
sentences.zh: 特别是希腊和罗马的历史，因为那只会助长对国王的反叛和革命。

sentences.en: And I think that everything that happens in the 18th century would have confirmed him in that view.
sentences.zh: 我认为18世纪发生的一切都印证了他的这一观点。

sentences.en: So, Robson-Pierre, like Charlotte Corday and like so many other stars of the revolution, is obsessed by classical history.
sentences.zh: 所以，罗伯斯庇尔，就像夏洛特·科黛以及革命中的许多其他明星一样，痴迷于古典历史。

sentences.en: He becomes a huge admirer of the virtues of the Greeks and the Romans, their love of country,
sentences.zh: 他极其崇拜希腊人和罗马人的美德、他们对祖国的热爱、

sentences.en: their determination not to allow their fellow citizens to succumb to conspiracies by evil aristocrats.
sentences.zh: 以及他们坚决不让同胞屈服于邪恶贵族阴谋的决心。

sentences.en: And the archetype of this is Cicero, provincial upstart who comes to Rome and saves his country from Catiline, who is the archetype of a seedy aristocratic conspirator.
sentences.zh: 这一切的典范就是西塞罗，一个来到罗马、拯救国家免受卡提那（一个肮脏的贵族阴谋家的典范）侵害的地方暴发户。

sentences.en: And he is obsessed by this in a way that so many people are.
sentences.zh: 他对此痴迷不已，就像许多人一样。

sentences.en: He takes it very seriously and he clearly identifies with Cicero very strongly.
sentences.zh: 他非常认真地对待这一点，并且显然对西塞罗有着极强的认同感。

sentences.en: But the person he really loves, again, a very familiar name throughout this entire series, is Rousseau, the favourite philosopher of an entire generation of revolutionaries.
sentences.zh: 但他真正热爱的人——同样，在整个系列中这是一个非常熟悉的名字——是卢梭，整整一代革命者最喜爱的哲学家。

sentences.en: And Robson-Pierre claimed that he had gone to visit Rousseau in 1778.
sentences.zh: 罗伯斯庇尔声称他在1778年去拜访过卢梭。

sentences.en: So, he wrote, I saw you in your last days and this memory is a source of proud joy for me.
sentences.zh: 因此他写道，我在你生命的最后日子里见到了你，这段记忆是我骄傲快乐的源泉。

sentences.en: So, scholars are unclear whether this is actually true or not.
sentences.zh: 所以，学者们并不清楚这究竟是不是真的。

sentences.en: Rousseau is about to die.
sentences.zh: 卢梭当时正要去世。

sentences.en: So, the only way that Robson-Pierre could have gone to see him, he's only 19, he would have had to skip school to go and see him.
sentences.zh: 所以，罗伯斯庇尔去看他的唯一可能方式——他当时才19岁——就是得逃学去看他。

sentences.en: So, there were lots of biographers of Robson-Pierre who think this is unlikely, but it's not impossible.
sentences.zh: 因此，许多罗伯斯庇尔的传记作者认为这不太可能，但也并非完全不可能。

sentences.en: And even if he made it up, I mean, it's kind of tribute to how passionately devoted to Rousseau-Rousseau-Pierre is.
sentences.zh: 而且即使他是编造的，我的意思是，这也某种程度上证明了他对卢梭是多么狂热和忠诚。

sentences.en: And the reason that he loves Rousseau is that Rousseau defines for Robson-Pierre the kind of the core principles that will underlie his politics throughout his entire life.
sentences.zh: 他热爱卢梭的原因在于，卢梭为罗伯斯庇尔界定了核心原则，这些原则将奠定他一生政治生涯的基础。

sentences.en: And there are really three key aspects of Rousseau's philosophy that Robson-Pierre comes to kind of treasure.
sentences.zh: 罗伯斯庇尔非常珍视卢梭哲学的三个核心方面。

sentences.en: And the ultimate one of these, the non-negotiable conviction that Robson-Pierre holds to throughout
sentences.zh: 其中最根本的一点，也是罗伯斯庇尔终其一生

sentences.en: his entire life, is that the common people are the absolute embodiment of virtue.
sentences.zh: 都坚守、绝不妥协的信念，就是普通民众是美德的绝对化身。

sentences.en: And if that is the case, then it follows, as Rousseau puts it, and this is the second principle that Robson-Pierre holds to, that the first of all laws is the well-being of the
sentences.zh: 如果是这样的话，那么正如卢梭所说——这也是罗伯斯庇尔坚守的第二个原则——一切法律的首要原则就是人民的

sentences.en: people.
sentences.zh: 福祉。

sentences.en: Nothing that does not contribute to the well-being of the people should be allowed in a virtuous state.
sentences.zh: 在美德之国中，任何无助于增进人民福祉的事物都不应被允许存在。

sentences.en: And that idealization of the people, capital P, so important to the French Revolution.
sentences.zh: 这种对人民（大写P）的理想化，对法国大革命至关重要。

sentences.en: We saw a little bit of a Marat, but Robson-Pierre even more so.
sentences.zh: 我们在马拉身上看到了一点影子，但在罗伯斯庇尔身上则更为明显。

sentences.en: Completely.
sentences.zh: 完全如此。

sentences.en: And what Robson-Pierre also holds to very passionately, and again, he gets this from Rousseau, is that
sentences.zh: 罗伯斯庇尔同样极其热忱地坚守的一点——同样也是从卢梭那里学来的——就是

sentences.en: history will throw up certain individuals who are peculiarly qualified to voice the will of the people, so the volonté générale, as Rousseau calls it, which in turn means that
sentences.zh: 历史会涌现出某些特定的人物，他们天生具备表达人民意志的资格，也就是卢梭所说的“公意”，这意味着

sentences.en: the will of the people isn't necessarily to be identified with the opinions of the majority.
sentences.zh: 人民的意志并不一定等同于多数人的意见。

sentences.en: Yeah, I love that.
sentences.zh: 是的，我很喜欢这一点。

sentences.en: So that's the very convenient.
sentences.zh: 所以这非常方便。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: The will of the people and what the majority of people think are two very different things.
sentences.zh: 人民的意志与大多数人的想法是两码事。

sentences.en: Yes, and this will be a trend on the left, I guess, throughout its subsequent history, that people on the far left, you might say, are often very impatient with the people for
sentences.zh: 是的，我想这也成了后来左翼运动的一种趋势，你可以说，极左翼人士往往对人民缺乏耐心，因为

sentences.en: not entirely corresponding to their sense of what the people should be.
sentences.zh: 人民并不完全符合他们心中“人民”应有的模样。

sentences.en: And Robson-Pierre identifies very strongly with this notion, and I think it's probably not pushing the psychologising too far to say that Robson-Pierre sees himself potentially
sentences.zh: 罗伯斯庇尔对这种观念有着强烈的共鸣，而且我认为，说罗伯斯庇尔潜在地把自己

sentences.en: as being such a person, someone who is qualified to articulate the will of the people.
sentences.zh: 看作这样一个人——一个有资格阐明人民意志的人——大概并不算过度心理分析。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: And actually, if you are the very bright boy who's a slightly unusual fit, but has been brought up among the people, that might give you a sense of combined loyalty to them, but
sentences.zh: 事实上，如果你是一个极其聪明的男孩，出身略显特殊，但又是在民众之中长大，这可能会让你产生一种对他们的复杂忠诚，但也

sentences.en: also perhaps a tiny element, I'm sure he would never have thought this himself, of contempt for their views, and a belief that he was better equipped to articulate what was good
sentences.zh: 可能带有一点点——我确信他自己绝不会这么想——对他们观点的轻蔑，并且坚信自己比他们自己更清楚什么对他们有益

sentences.en: for them than they are themselves, don't you think?
sentences.zh: ，你不觉得吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm sure he would never have thought of that consciously.
sentences.zh: 是的，我确信他绝不会有意识地这样想。

sentences.en: No, but unconsciously, he thinks, I know them, they are not maybe the best judges of their own best interests, but I do care about them, and I am better equipped.
sentences.zh: 不，但在潜意识里他会想：我了解他们，他们或许不是自身最佳利益的最佳判断者，但我确实关心他们，而且我更有能力。

sentences.en: I really understand them in a way they don't understand themselves.
sentences.zh: 我以他们自己无法理解的方式真正理解他们。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a pre-Marxist version of worrying about the false consciousness that the working
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是马克思主义诞生前的一种版本，担忧着劳动群众

sentences.en: masses have, and that perhaps it takes a brilliant intellectual to penetrate this and to see what really matters, and that the mass of the people are unqualified to do that.
sentences.zh: 所拥有的虚假意识，认为或许需要一个 brilhante 的知识分子来洞察这一点，看出真正重要的是什么，而广大民众则不具备这种能力。

sentences.en: And I do think that Robson-Pierre kind of sees himself in those terMs.
sentences.zh: 我确实认为罗伯斯庇尔正是从这些角度看待自己的。

sentences.en: And this is, I think, what explains why when the French Revolution erupts in 1789, he is desperate to be a part of it.
sentences.zh: 我想，这正是为什么当1789年法国大革命爆发时，他渴望置身其中的原因。

sentences.en: So Ruth Skur, who wrote another biography of Robson-Pierre, Fatal Purity, which is wonderfully
sentences.zh: 因此，写过另一部罗伯斯庇尔传记《致命纯洁》的露丝·斯库尔，其文笔精彩绝伦

sentences.en: well-written, his recognition of this opportunity and the ferocity of his determination to see it was amazing.
sentences.zh: ，他对比机会的敏锐洞察以及决心把握机会的狠劲是惊人的。

sentences.en: He is determined to go to Versailles, to be part of this great assembly of the various estates that Louis XVI has summoned.
sentences.zh: 他决心前往凡尔赛，成为路易十六召集的各等级国民议会的一部分。

sentences.en: And so he does, he gets elected.
sentences.zh: 于是他去了，他当选了。

sentences.en: He goes to Versailles as an elected representative of the people of his hometown.
sentences.zh: 他作为家乡人民的民选代表前往凡尔赛。

sentences.en: But he is, even though he's an elected representative, he is, of course, relative to
sentences.zh: 但尽管他是一名民选代表，相对于

sentences.en: lots of other people who are assembling in Versailles, basically a nobody.
sentences.zh: 汇聚在凡尔赛的许多其他人来说，他基本上是个无名小卒。

sentences.en: I mean, he's very earneSt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他非常认真。

sentences.en: He's very stiff.
sentences.zh: 他非常古板。

sentences.en: He seems to be without much charisma at all.
sentences.zh: 他似乎毫无个人魅力可言。

sentences.en: And yet, over the course of the four years that follow the eruption of the revolution, he emerges to become one of the most celebrated figures in revolutionary France, admired and
sentences.zh: 然而，在革命爆发后的四年里，他脱颖而出，成为了革命的法国最受瞩目的人物之一，既备受爱戴

sentences.en: hated in equal measure.
sentences.zh: 又饱受唾弃。

sentences.en: And the measure of his rise to power is something that you mentioned in your previous episode,
sentences.zh: 正如你在上一集节目中提到的那样，多米尼克，他崛起掌握权力的标志是

sentences.en: Dominic, that on the 27th of July, 1793, France is seemingly on the verge of disintegration.
sentences.zh: 1793年7月27日，法国似乎已经到了崩溃的边缘。

sentences.en: Robespierre is elected to this proto-dictatorial body, the Committee of Public Safety.
sentences.zh: 罗伯斯庇尔当选进入了这个具有准独裁性质的机构——公共安全委员会。

sentences.en: And this means that he is now one of 10 men, soon to be 12, who have been appointed to protect
sentences.zh: 这意味着他现在是最初10人（不久后扩充到12人）委员会的一员，他们的职责是

sentences.en: the nation from invasion, from counter-revolution, from economic collapse, and in effect, try and save the revolution from imploding totally.
sentences.zh: 保护国家免受外敌入侵、反革命颠覆、经济崩溃的影响，实际上是试图拯救濒临彻底崩溃的革命。

sentences.en: And why him?
sentences.zh: 为什么是他？

sentences.en: I mean, what, you know, we described him, very prim, very well read, maybe a little bit priggish, not exactly an obvious man for a national military and economic emergency.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们之前形容过他，非常古板、博览群书、或许有点清高，怎么看也不像是应对国家军事和经济紧急状况的合适人选。

sentences.en: So what are the qualities that have led Robespierre to the top?
sentences.zh: 那么，是什么特质将罗伯斯庇尔推上了顶峰？

sentences.en: What do people see in him?
sentences.zh: 人们在他身上看到了什么？

sentences.en: Well, I think there are two in particular, and both of these have been on public display from his earliest days as a lawyer back in Arras.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为主要有两个特质，这两点从他早年在阿拉斯当律师时起就一直在公众面前展现出来。

sentences.en: And the first of these is that he displays a remarkable consistency of principle.
sentences.zh: 首先，他表现出了一种非凡的原则一致性。

sentences.en: From the earliest days, he is kind of unswerving in his opinions.
sentences.zh: 从一开始，他在观点上就坚定不移。

sentences.en: He doesn't trim, he doesn't tap, he doesn't alter them.
sentences.zh: 他不左右逢源，不妥协退让，也从不改变立场。

sentences.en: And these principles are essentially a completely resolute commitment to popular sovereignty, to the will of the people.
sentences.zh: 这些原则本质上是对人民主权和人民意志的绝对坚定承诺。

sentences.en: A profound sympathy for the people, a sense of identification with them, and an opposition to autocratic government.
sentences.zh: 对人民怀有深切的同情，有着强烈的认同感，并坚决反对专制政府。

sentences.en: And the consistency with which he holds these principles makes him seem to both his friends and indeed his enemies very unusual.
sentences.zh: 他坚守这些原则的一致性，让他的朋友乃至敌人都觉得他非常与众不同。

sentences.en: And it gives him a kind of austere reputation.
sentences.zh: 这也赋予了他一种严肃刚正的名声。

sentences.en: Even those who dislike him are forced to respect him.
sentences.zh: 即使是那些不喜欢他的人也不得不尊重他。

sentences.en: And this is then combined with an absolute commitment to his own ferociously high moral standards.
sentences.zh: 这一点与他对自身极其严格的高标准道德的绝对承诺结合在了一起。

sentences.en: He is unbribable.
sentences.zh: 他是一块无法收买的硬骨头。

sentences.en: And again, this makes him pretty much unique among all the various French revolutionaries.
sentences.zh: 同样，这使他在所有形形色色的法国革命者中几乎独一无二。

sentences.en: Obvious contrast is with Danton, who is cheerfully, cheerfully corrupt.
sentences.zh: 最明显的对比就是丹东，他是个快活且毫不掩饰的腐败分子。

sentences.en: But basically, everyone is pocketing bribes left, right and centre.
sentences.zh: 但基本上，所有的人都在四处大肆收受贿赂。

sentences.en: Robespierre never does.
sentences.zh: 而罗伯斯庇尔从不这么做。

sentences.en: And again, this makes him seem so unusual to his admirers as to kind of make him seem a unique figure.
sentences.zh: 同样，这让他的崇拜者觉得他如此与众不同，仿佛是一个独一无二的人物。

sentences.en: And again, it's kind of redolent of Plutarch, this idea of the heroes of the early Roman Republic,
sentences.zh: 这也让人联想起普鲁塔克笔下早期罗马共和国英雄的形象

sentences.en: people who are completely austere in their personal habits, completely committed to principles of moral virtue.
sentences.zh: ——那些个人生活极为简朴、对道德美德原则坚定不移的人。

sentences.en: And he serves, I think, the revolution as a model of what civic and revolutionary virtue could be and can be.
sentences.zh: 我认为，他为大革命树立了一个公民与革命美德应有样板的典范。

sentences.en: And ever since May 1791, he's been given this magnificent nickname, the incorruptible.
sentences.zh: 从1791年5月起，他就被赋予了这个响亮的绰号：不可腐蚀者。

sentences.en: And maybe this takes us back to his dress, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 也许这让我们想到了他的穿着，对吧？

sentences.en: Because, I mean, you're talking about his consistency.
sentences.zh: 因为，我是说，你在谈论他的始终如一。

sentences.en: Everybody else has changed what they – I mean, they've changed their principles, they've changed their politics, they've changed their factions,
sentences.zh: 其他所有人都改变了他们——我的意思是，他们改变了原则，改变了政治立场，改变了派系，

sentences.en: and they've changed their clothes to go along with it.
sentences.zh: 并且为了顺应潮流连衣服都换了。

sentences.en: Yes, he's always been himself, and he'll never change.
sentences.zh: 是的，他一直是他自己，而且他永远不会改变。

sentences.en: Hence the stockings, I guess.
sentences.zh: 所以我想这就是为什么他穿长袜。

sentences.en: He is not a man who is going to give up the fashions that he likes just to demonstrate his virtue.
sentences.zh: 他绝不是那种为了证明自己的美德而放弃喜爱的时尚的人。

sentences.en: He doesn't need to do that.
sentences.zh: 他不需要那样做。

sentences.en: His virtue should be self-evident.
sentences.zh: 他的美德应当是不言自明的。

sentences.en: And because he is seen as such an admirable person, he is the incorruptible.
sentences.zh: 正因为他被视为如此令人钦佩的人，他才被称为“不可腐蚀者”。

sentences.en: This reputation is going to prove an incredible asset for the Committee of Public Safety,
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这种声誉将成为公共安全委员会的一笔惊人财富，

sentences.en: because it serves as an assurance to good citizens everywhere that the Committee shares in Robespierre's own moral probity.
sentences.zh: 因为它向各地的好公民保证，委员会拥有与罗伯斯庇尔相同的道德正直。

sentences.en: Robespierre's kind of complete commitment to the procedures of the Committee, to its workings, is evident from the moment that he joins it.
sentences.zh: 罗伯斯庇尔对委员会程序和运作的全身心投入，从他加入的那一刻起就显而易见了。

sentences.en: So he attends all its meetings assiduously.
sentences.zh: 因此，他勤勉地出席每一次会议。

sentences.en: He goes in at seven o'clock in the morning to read and respond to dispatches.
sentences.zh: 他清晨七点就去阅读并回复公文。

sentences.en: He returns after a long day of business at eight o'clock in the evening.
sentences.zh: 结束了一天漫长的工作后，他在晚上八点返回。

sentences.en: He often stays late into the night.
sentences.zh: 他常常深夜才离去。

sentences.en: And this is a huge commitment.
sentences.zh: 这是一个巨大的承诺。

sentences.en: And it means that with Robespierre as the kind of example of what these Committee members are expected to do,
sentences.zh: 这意味着，以罗伯斯庇尔作为委员会成员应当效仿的榜样，

sentences.en: the Committee very rapidly becomes the kind of beating heart of the Revolution.
sentences.zh: 委员会迅速成为了革命的核心跳动动力。

sentences.en: So its meetings are held in this green papered room in the Pavillon de Flore, which is a 17th century building that connected to Tuileries,
sentences.zh: 因此，会议在花神宫（Pavillon de Flore）一间贴着绿色墙纸的房间里举行，这是一座连接着杜伊勒里宫的17世纪建筑，

sentences.en: where the Convention had its kind of headquarters in the Louvre.
sentences.zh: 国民公会曾把总部设在卢浮宫里。

sentences.en: And inevitably, the Pavillon de Flore has been renamed.
sentences.zh: 不可避免地，花神宫被重新命名了。

sentences.en: It's become the Pavillon de l'Egalité, the Pavilion of Equality.
sentences.zh: 它变成了平等宫（Pavillon de l'Egalité）。

sentences.en: And this room with its green wallpaper is basically now the nerve centre of the Revolution.
sentences.zh: 这个贴着绿色墙纸的房间基本上成了现在革命的神经中枢。

sentences.en: And the mood in it is incredibly febrile.
sentences.zh: 那里的气氛异常狂热。

sentences.en: It's fraught.
sentences.zh: 充满紧张。

sentences.en: It's anxious.
sentences.zh: 令人焦虑。

sentences.en: The average age of the Committee members is 30.
sentences.zh: 委员会成员的平均年龄是30岁。

sentences.en: They're often absolutely tanked up on drink.
sentences.zh: 他们往往喝得酩酊大醉。

sentences.en: There's a general mood of panic.
sentences.zh: 弥漫着一种普遍的恐慌情绪。

sentences.en: As well, there might be, because basically everything that could go wrong seems to be going wrong.
sentences.zh: 这也是理所当然的，因为基本上所有可能出错的事情似乎都在出错。

sentences.en: So we talked about it in the previous episode.
sentences.zh: 我们在上一集里讨论过这一点。

sentences.en: Military crisis, civil war, inflation, bread shortages.
sentences.zh: 军事危机、内战、通货膨胀、面包短缺。

sentences.en: Dominic, it's like Britain in 1974.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，这就像1974年的英国。

sentences.en: That's fantastic, Tom.
sentences.zh: 太棒了，汤姆。

sentences.en: That's a great comparison.
sentences.zh: 这是一个极好的比喻。

sentences.en: You're welcome.
sentences.zh: 不客气。

sentences.en: Who's Marcy Williams in this analogy?
sentences.zh: 在这场类比中，谁是马西·威廉姆斯？

sentences.en: The Incorruptible doesn't have a Marcy WilliaMs.
sentences.zh: “不可腐蚀者”可没有马西·威廉姆斯。

sentences.en: No, he doesn't.
sentences.zh: 不，他没有。

sentences.en: He's above all that.
sentences.zh: 他超然物外。

sentences.en: I mean, his incorruptibility is so useful at the time when people are looking for traitors, because he is the one person nobody would ever suspect of being a traitor.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在人们到处寻找叛徒的时候，他的清廉是如此有用，因为他是唯一一个谁都不会怀疑是叛徒的人。

sentences.en: I mean, at a point when you're saying, you know, Dumourier, the Girondin, whoever, behind the mask, they were actually plotting all along.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当你在说，你知道的，迪穆里埃、吉伦特派，无论谁，他们摘下面具后其实一直在密谋。

sentences.en: Finally, we found a bloke that nobody would ever, ever say that about.
sentences.zh: 最后，我们找到了一个谁也绝对不会这么说的人。

sentences.en: But he's not just there as a sort of as a mascot, is he?
sentences.zh: 但他不仅仅是作为某种吉祥物坐在那里的，对吧？

sentences.en: He is there because he he has an idea of the way out of the crisis that is going to become incredibly potent in the next few weeks and months.
sentences.zh: 他坐在那里是因为他有一个摆脱危机的想法，这将在未来几周和几个月内变得极其强大。

sentences.en: Yeah, so he has an explanation for what's been going wrong.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以他对出错的原因有一个解释。

sentences.en: But even more crucially, he has a solution.
sentences.zh: 但更关键的是，他有一个解决方案。

sentences.en: So when you're in the midst of a crisis, you want someone who can give you what seems a plausible way out of it.
sentences.zh: 因此，当你身处危机之中时，你会希望有人能为你提供一个看似可行的出路。

sentences.en: And this is what Robespierre does.
sentences.zh: 这就是罗伯斯庇尔所做的。

sentences.en: And it gradually enables him over the course of the weeks and the months that follow his ascension to the committee to take on an ever more preponderant role in it.
sentences.zh: 这使得他在加入委员会后几周乃至几个月的进程中，逐渐在其中扮演了越来越主导的角色。

sentences.en: And it will turn out that Robespierre isn't just a man of the utmost moral probity, not just a man with an unrivaled insight into the pathologies of the revolution, but also,
sentences.zh: 事实证明，罗伯斯庇尔不仅是一个道德堪称楷模的人，不仅是一个对革命病理有着无与伦比洞察力的人，而且，

sentences.en: crucially, a man who is absolutely brilliant at politics and, in fact, probably better at politics than any other revolutionary in France.
sentences.zh: 至关重要的是，他还是一个精通政治的天才，事实上，他的政治手腕可能比法国任何其他革命者都要高明。

sentences.en: Crikey, that's a big claim.
sentences.zh: 天哪，这可真是个惊人的断言。

sentences.en: Well, we'll come back after the break and Tom will justify this extraordinary claim.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们休息一会儿再回来，由汤姆来为这个非凡的断言辩护。

sentences.en: This episode is supported by Anthropic, the team behind Claude.
sentences.zh: 本节目由 Claude 的幕后团队 Anthropic 赞助支持。

sentences.en: Now, history's biggest leaps, many of them started as hard questions that people didn't want asked.
sentences.zh: 历史上的许多重大飞跃，最初都是从人们不愿去问的艰难问题开始的。

sentences.en: Yeah, there's a classic example of that, Tom, at the end of the 15th century.
sentences.zh: 是的，汤姆，15世纪末就有一个经典的例子。

sentences.en: And the hard question in particular was what is out there beyond the Atlantic Ocean to the West?
sentences.zh: 而那个特殊的高难度问题是：大西洋西岸的彼端究竟有什么？

sentences.en: And as you will know, the man who found the answer to that question was the explorer Christopher Columbus.
sentences.zh: 正如你所知，找到这个问题答案的人是探险家克里斯托弗·哥伦布。

sentences.en: Great pioneering voyage of discovery.
sentences.zh: 伟大的开创性发现之旅。

sentences.en: And he is, of course, the Americas.
sentences.zh: 当然，他发现了美洲。

sentences.en: So, you know, Anthropic knows the importance of questions.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，Anthropic 深知问题的重要性。

sentences.en: And it's why Anthropic is founded on one hard question above all.
sentences.zh: 这也是 Anthropic 建立在一个最核心的高难度问题之上的原因。

sentences.en: How can we ensure that the AI revolution really goes well for ordinary people?
sentences.zh: 我们如何确保人工智能革命真正能给普通人带来美好的未来？
