sentences.en: Let's zoom in on one house in Paris.
sentences.zh: 让我们把镜头聚焦到巴黎的一栋房子。

sentences.en: In the Rue Saint-Honoré.
sentences.zh: 位于圣奥诺雷街（Rue Saint-Honoré）。

sentences.en: It's a small two-story house.
sentences.zh: 这是一栋两层的小房子。

sentences.en: It's a few minutes walk away from the Jacobin Club.
sentences.zh: 距离雅各宾俱乐部步行只需几分钟。

sentences.en: Where the radicals meet in the convent of the Jacobin.
sentences.zh: 激进分子在雅各宾修道院开会的地方。

sentences.en: And this is the house where a cabinet maker lives called Maurice Dupley and his family.
sentences.zh: 这就是一位名叫莫里斯·迪普莱的细木工及其家人的住所。

sentences.en: He's a joiner.
sentences.zh: 他是一名木匠。

sentences.en: And he's also a very keen radical.
sentences.zh: 他也是一个非常热心的激进分子。

sentences.en: And he has a lodger.
sentences.zh: 他有一个房客。

sentences.en: And the name of that lodger is, of course, Maximilien Robespierre.
sentences.zh: 那个房客的名字自然就是马克西米利安·罗伯斯庇尔。
zh_words: 马克西米利安·罗伯斯庇尔

sentences.en: And Tom has been there for two years.
sentences.zh: 汤姆已经在那里住了两年了。

sentences.en: And he loves it, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 他很喜欢那里，不是吗？

sentences.en: He loves the Dupleys.
sentences.zh: 他很喜欢迪普莱一家。

sentences.en: He does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: He admires Maurice Dupley as a kind of example of the working classes for whom Robespierre is fighting.
sentences.zh: 他将莫里斯·迪普莱视为罗伯斯庇尔正在为之战斗的工人阶级的榜样。

sentences.en: But also, there is a Madame Dupley and she has three daughters and they just fuss and fuss over Robespierre.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，迪普莱夫人有三个女儿，她们对罗伯斯庇尔关怀备至、嘘寒问暖。

sentences.en: And he absolutely adores this.
sentences.zh: 而他极其享受这一切。

sentences.en: So to quote Charlotte, his sister, who was actually very jealous of the women in the Dupley family.
sentences.zh: 引用他的妹妹夏洛特的话说，她其实非常嫉妒迪普莱一家的女性。

sentences.en: They expressed towards him the most vivid interest and surrounded him with their thousand delicate concerns.
sentences.zh: 她们向他表达了最热烈的情意，并用她们千般温柔的关怀将他团团围住。

sentences.en: He was extremely susceptible to all these sorts of things.
sentences.zh: 他极易受到所有这类事情的影响。

sentences.en: So he doesn't just have one Marcia Williams, he's got three.
sentences.zh: 所以他不仅有一个玛西亚·威廉姆斯，他有三个。

sentences.en: But his relationship with them is above suspicion.
sentences.zh: 但他与她们的关系无可挑剔。

sentences.en: So pure.
sentences.zh: 如此纯洁。

sentences.en: Purely platonic.
sentences.zh: 纯粹是柏拉图式的。

sentences.en: And his own room is very, very Spartan, which is exactly how he likes it.
sentences.zh: 而他自己的房间非常非常简朴，这正是他喜欢的风格。

sentences.en: So there's a bed, there's a writing table, there's some bookshelves, absolutely nothing else.
sentences.zh: 所以里面有一张床、一张写字台、一些书架，绝对没有别的东西。

sentences.en: So it is, you know, a suitably ascetic retreat for the incorruptible.
sentences.zh: 所以你知道，这是一个适合廉洁之人的苦行隐修所。

sentences.en: Nobody ever hints at any impropriety in Robespierre's relationship with the women of the Dupley family.
sentences.zh: 没有人会暗示罗伯斯庇尔与迪普莱一家的女性之间有任何不当关系。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Just going to emphasise that.
sentences.zh: 我只是想强调这一点。

sentences.en: So he's in his room and that evening he sits down at his desk and he ponders the terrible crisis that is facing France and the revolution.
sentences.zh: 所以他在房间里，那天晚上他坐在书桌前，思考着摆在法国和革命面前的可怕危机。

sentences.en: So there are foreign armies on French soil, the Austrians, the Prussians.
sentences.zh: 法国本土有外国军队，奥地利人和普鲁士人。

sentences.en: There is a British naval blockade.
sentences.zh: 还有英国的海上封锁。

sentences.en: There is a mass insurrection in Vendée.
sentences.zh: 旺代发生了大规模暴动。

sentences.en: We heard about that in the last episode.
sentences.zh: 我们在上一集里听说过。

sentences.en: There are counter-revolutionary uprisings, federalist uprisings, historians call them, in cities that include Lyon, Marseille, and crucially the great naval base of Toulon,
sentences.zh: 还有反革命起义，历史学家称之为联邦主义者起义，发生里昂、马赛等地，最关键的是还有伟大的海军基地土伦，

sentences.en: where the British Navy is hovering on the margins.
sentences.zh: 英国海军就在附近盘旋。

sentences.en: And of course, there are food shortages in Paris.
sentences.zh: 当然，巴黎还面临粮食短缺。

sentences.en: And so there are demonstrations in the streets all the time.
sentences.zh: 所以街头总是不断爆发示威活动。

sentences.en: Robespierre contemplates this and then he draws up, well, let's call it a catechism.
sentences.zh: 罗伯斯庇尔思考了这些，然后拟定了一份——嗯，我们姑且称之为教义问答的东西。

sentences.en: You know, the kind of the religious quality of the most radical revolutionaries, I think, is very evident.
sentences.zh: 我认为，最激进的革命者身上那种宗教般的特质非常明显。

sentences.en: And this is an example.
sentences.zh: 这就是一个例子。

sentences.en: And what Robespierre is trying to do is to define the precise challenges that he will be facing as a member of the Committee of Public Safety,
sentences.zh: 罗伯斯庇尔试图做的是，明确他作为救国委员会成员将要面临的具体挑战，

sentences.en: which he's going to be joining the following day.
sentences.zh: 他第二天就要加入这个委员会。

sentences.en: And so he writes, question, what is our aim?
sentences.zh: 于是他写道，问题：我们的目标是什么？

sentences.en: Answer, to provide governance for the benefit of the people.
sentences.zh: 回答：为了人民的利益进行治理。

sentences.en: And the people, of course, for Robespierre are the great embodiment of virtue.
sentences.zh: 当然，对罗伯斯庇尔来说，人民是美德的伟大化身。

sentences.en: And this is a principle that he's absorbed from Rousseau and which he will never abandon.
sentences.zh: 这是他从卢梭那里吸收并永远不会放弃的原则。

sentences.en: This assumption that the poor are intrinsically good.
sentences.zh: 这种假设认为穷人本质上是善良的。

sentences.en: They can do no wrong.
sentences.zh: 他们不会犯错。

sentences.en: But there is a problem, which is that France is facing massive popular insurrections in the provinces.
sentences.zh: 但问题在于，法国各省正面临大规模的人民起义。

sentences.en: And so this requires Robespierre to answer an obvious question.
sentences.zh: 因此，这要求罗伯斯庇尔回答一个显而易见的问题。

sentences.en: If the people are intrinsically good, why are they behaving in such a way?
sentences.zh: 如果人民本质上是善良的，他们为什么会这样表现？

sentences.en: Why are they refusing to behave in a kind of the selfless and patriotic manner that they probably should be if they are intrinsically virtuous?
sentences.zh: 如果他们本质上是有美德的，他们为什么拒绝表现出本该具备的那种无私和爱国主义精神？

sentences.en: And Robespierre's answer to this puzzle is that they are being kept in ignorance and poverty by the rich and the corrupt.
sentences.zh: 罗伯斯庇尔对这个谜题的解答是，他们是被富人和腐败分子灌输了无知和贫困。

sentences.en: So it's a sort of version of our old friend, false consciousness,
sentences.zh: 所以这有点像是我们老朋友“虚假意识”的一个版本，

sentences.en: but one that has been much more deliberately and malevolently contrived by this coalition of the enemies of France.
sentences.zh: 但这是一种由法国敌人的这个联盟更加刻意、更加恶毒地策划出来的版本。

sentences.en: And specifically of the poor.
sentences.zh: 特别是针对穷人的敌人。

sentences.en: So he's saying, you know, who are the chief obstacles to the enlightenment of the poor?
sentences.zh: 所以他说，你知道，谁是启迪穷人的主要障碍？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The paid journalists who mislead them every day by shameless distortions.
sentences.zh: 那些每天用无耻的歪曲误导他们的受薪记者。

sentences.en: I'm very familiar with that argument, I have to say.
sentences.zh: 我不得不说，我对这种论调非常熟悉。

sentences.en: So in other words, if only people weren't reading awful columnists in the Daily Mail, everything would be perfect.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，要是人们不去看《每日邮报》上那些糟糕的专栏作家的文章，一切就完美了。

sentences.en: That's absolutely Robespierre's vibe.
sentences.zh: 这完全就是罗伯斯庇尔的调调。

sentences.en: Robespierre also blames turncoat generals like Lafayette and Desmauriers, both of whom have defected from the revolution to foreign enemies.
sentences.zh: 罗伯斯庇尔还谴责了像拉法耶特和迪穆里埃这样的叛徒将军，他们两人都背叛了革命，投奔了外国敌人。

sentences.en: The British, who Robespierre describes as an insolent and vile people, and particularly their prime minister, William Pitt,
sentences.zh: 英国人——罗伯斯庇尔将他们描述为傲慢而卑鄙的人民，特别是他们的首相小威廉·皮特，

sentences.en: who is seen as flooding France with gold and the temptation to blame everything that is happening on France on Pitt's gold is a very strong one to which revolutionaries will repeatedly succumb.
sentences.zh: 他被视为用黄金淹没法国，而把法国发生的一切都归咎于皮特的黄金，这种诱惑非常强大，革命者会屡次向其屈服。

sentences.en: And Robespierre also blames traitors and conspirators.
sentences.zh: 罗伯斯庇尔还将责任归咎于叛徒和阴谋家。

sentences.en: And these are perhaps the most pernicious enemies of all, because these are monsters who wear the show of patriotism,
sentences.zh: 这些也许是最危险的敌人，因为这些是披着爱国主义外衣的怪物，

sentences.en: but who secretly beneath the surface are working for the overthrow of the revolution.
sentences.zh: 但他们在背地里却暗中为推翻革命而工作。

sentences.en: And just on that, here's a mad thing.
sentences.zh: 说到这里，有一件疯狂的事。

sentences.en: It is often said in the final months of 1793, early 1794, the more keen somebody appears to be on the revolution, the more likely it is that they are a traitor.
sentences.zh: 人们常说，在1793年的最后几个月到1794年初，一个人表现得对革命越狂热，他越有可能是个叛徒。

sentences.en: They're protesting too much.
sentences.zh: 他们辩解得太多了。

sentences.en: And so Robespierre draws up this list of all the enemies that France is facing, and he comes to the conclusion that all these perils,
sentences.zh: 于是，罗伯斯庇尔列出了法国面临的所有敌人这份名单，他得出的结论是，所有这些危险，

sentences.en: they're not just a kind of concatenation of distinct and separate crises,
sentences.zh: 并不仅仅是一系列独立且分离的危机的简单叠加，

sentences.en: but rather the expression of a kind of omni-crisis, you might call it, a singular conspiracy that has multiple tentacles,
sentences.zh: 而是某种“全危机”（你可以这么称呼它）的体现，即一个有着多只触手的单一阴谋，

sentences.en: and that these tentacles are reaching out to throttle the revolution wherever it can get a grip.
sentences.zh: 这些触手四处伸展，试图在任何能够得着的地方扼杀革命。

sentences.en: And there is a clarity to this perspective, a kind of a purity and starkness, which when he goes to join the Committee of Public Safety and presents it to them,
sentences.zh: 这种视角具有一种清晰度，一种纯粹和严峻，当他去加入救国委员会并向他们展示这一点时，

sentences.en: his fellow members find very appealing.
sentences.zh: 他的同僚们觉得非常有吸引力。

sentences.en: And in fact, probably this is why they've co-opted him.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这可能就是他们拉拢他的原因。

sentences.en: Well, this idea of the omni-conspiracy, you know, that everything is related and that absolutely everything comes back to this conspiracy.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这个“全面阴谋”的概念，你知道的，即一切都是息息相关的，绝对每件事都可以追溯到这个阴谋。

sentences.en: This is going to run through this episode and the next four episodes.
sentences.zh: 这将贯穿这一集和接下来的四集。

sentences.en: You know, this is what explains his motivation and that of some of his colleagues, that they genuinely believe it, don't they?
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就是他的动机以及他的一些同僚的动机之所在，他们是真心相信这一点的，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: They have fallen down the YouTube rabbit hole, and they genuinely think that these people, these people, these people, who actually don't know each other at all,
sentences.zh: 他们掉进了YouTube的阴谋论兔子洞，并且真心认为这群人、那群人、还有那些人——他们实际上根本互不相识——

sentences.en: are all working in one plot, and actually William Pierce is paying for it.
sentences.zh: 都在参与同一个阴谋，而且实际上是小威廉·皮特在出资赞助。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's exactly what he thinks.
sentences.zh: 是的，他就是这么想的。

sentences.en: And because of his moral reputation and because of the clarity with which he expresses it, I mean, he doesn't,
sentences.zh: 正因为他的道德声誉，也正因为他表达这种观点的清晰度——我是说，他并没有，

sentences.en: he's not accepted immediately as the leader of the committee and his fellow members don't agree with him on every point.
sentences.zh: 他并没有立刻被接受为委员会的领导人，他的同僚们也并非在所有问题上都赞同他。

sentences.en: But it does mean that his understanding of the crisis facing the revolution and what it's taken to fight it becomes increasingly influential.
sentences.zh: 但这确实意味着，他对革命所面临的危机以及战胜危机所需付出的代价的理解，正变得越来越具有影响力。

sentences.en: Well, it's very simple.
sentences.zh: 这很简单。

sentences.en: It's very simple.
sentences.zh: 非常简单。

sentences.en: It's very attractive.
sentences.zh: 非常有吸引力。

sentences.en: Yeah, because a simple policy is always the most welcome.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为简单的政策总是最受欢迎的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: You don't want to faff around with dealing with multiple contingencies.
sentences.zh: 你肯定不想为应付各种突发情况而手忙脚乱。

sentences.en: You want a nice, clear answer that explains everything.
sentences.zh: 你想要一个清晰明了、能解释一切的答案。

sentences.en: Completely.
sentences.zh: 完全赞同。

sentences.en: And so there are two men on the committee in particular who are massive Robespierre fans.
sentences.zh: 委员会里有两个人，特别迷罗伯斯庇尔。

sentences.en: And let's just look at them because they're going to play an important role in the story that we're going to be telling over the course of the terror.
sentences.zh: 让我们来看看他们，因为在我们接下来要讲述的恐怖统治故事中，他们将扮演重要角色。

sentences.en: So the first of these, Dominic, you quoted him several times in episode one.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，这其中的第一个人，你在第一集里引用过他好几次。

sentences.en: It's a guy called Georges Couton.
sentences.zh: 这家伙叫乔治·库东。

sentences.en: So he's 38, so three years older than Robespierre when Robespierre joins the committee.
sentences.zh: 他当时38岁，比罗伯斯庇尔加入委员会时大三岁。

sentences.en: And he's a lawyer from the Averne in the south of France.
sentences.zh: 他是一名来自法国南部奥弗涅的律师。

sentences.en: And all his life he had suffered from bad joints, bad sinews.
sentences.zh: 他一辈子都饱受关节和肌腱疼痛的折磨。

sentences.en: And unfortunately, by 1793, he's effectively paralysed below the waiSt.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，到了1793年，他基本上腰部以下瘫痪了。

sentences.en: So he's confined to a wheelchair.
sentences.zh: 所以他只能坐轮椅。

sentences.en: And what had caused this, his doctors had diagnosed meningitis.
sentences.zh: 医生诊断导致这种情况的原因是脑膜炎。

sentences.en: But Couton himself blamed this condition on having had too much sex as a young man.
sentences.zh: 但库东自己却把这归咎于年轻时性生活过度。

sentences.en: And whether he says that because it sounds slightly more glamorous explanation for his condition than meningitis, I don't know whether he genuinely believed it.
sentences.zh: 我不知道他这么说，是因为比起脑膜炎，这听起来更带点传奇色彩，还是他真的相信这一点。

sentences.en: Did that weaken his joints?
sentences.zh: 这会削弱他的关节吗？

sentences.en: Did that also explain the bad joints?
sentences.zh: 这也解释了关节不好的原因吗？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I wasn't aware that was a consequence of it, but maybe it is.
sentences.zh: 我以前不知道这也是个后果，不过也许吧。

sentences.en: Listeners can absorb that lesson as they wish.
sentences.zh: 听众们可以自行领会这个教训。

sentences.en: I mean, you think he's a lovely man, don't you, this guy Couton?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你觉得他是个可爱的人，对吧，这个叫库东的家伙？

sentences.en: I don't.
sentences.zh: 我不觉得。

sentences.en: I'm reporting the general consensus on Couton, which is people find him very, in private, charming, affable.
sentences.zh: 我只是在转述大家对库东的普遍看法，那就是私下里人们觉得他非常迷人、随和。

sentences.en: Like Robespierre, he's a bit of a sentimentaliSt.
sentences.zh: 和罗伯斯庇尔一样，他也有点多愁善感。

sentences.en: But unlike Robespierre, he has a sense of humour.
sentences.zh: 但与罗伯斯庇尔不同的是，他很有幽默感。

sentences.en: He's a fun person to be with.
sentences.zh: 和他在一起很有趣。

sentences.en: So he's a funster.
sentences.zh: 所以他是个开心果。

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: He's a funster.
sentences.zh: 他是个开心果。

sentences.en: But as a politician, he completely buys into Robespierre's diagnosis and the cure.
sentences.zh: 但作为一名政治家，他完全接受了罗伯斯庇尔的诊断和疗方。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The other big Robespierre fan on the committee is perhaps the most glamorous of all its members.
sentences.zh: 委员会里另一个狂热的罗伯斯庇尔崇拜者，或许也是所有成员中最耀眼的一个。

sentences.en: And this is a guy who's only 25.
sentences.zh: 这家伙年仅25岁。

sentences.en: So the baby of the committee.
sentences.zh: 可以说是委员会里的老幺。

sentences.en: And this is a guy called Louis Antoine de Saint-JuSt.
sentences.zh: 这个人叫路易·安托万·德·圣茹斯特。
zh_words: 路易·安托万·德·圣茹斯特

sentences.en: And he's very dandyish, very handsome, kind of rock star vibe.
sentences.zh: 他非常讲究穿着，长相英俊，有种摇滚明星的气质。

sentences.en: He's like a kind of young Mick Jagger.
sentences.zh: 他就像个年轻的米克·贾格尔。

sentences.en: Long hair.
sentences.zh: 长发飘飘。

sentences.en: Long hair.
sentences.zh: 长发。

sentences.en: Loves to sing an Italian aria.
sentences.zh: 喜欢唱意大利咏叹调。

sentences.en: He's always doing that.
sentences.zh: 他总是这样。

sentences.en: But he's also very, very chill, very self-disciplined, implacably committed to his values, to his beliefs in a very Robespierre fashion.
sentences.zh: 但他也非常冷静、极具自律，以罗伯斯庇尔的方式坚定不移地忠于自己的价值观和信念。

sentences.en: And in fact, he has been very influenced by Robespierre.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他深受罗伯斯庇尔的影响。

sentences.en: So he had written to the great man back in 1790, actually, when Robespierre wasn't really a great man.
sentences.zh: 早在1790年，他就给这位伟人写过信，当时罗伯斯庇尔还算不上什么伟人。

sentences.en: He kind of talent spotted him at a very early age.
sentences.zh: 他很早就慧眼识珠相中了罗伯斯庇尔。

sentences.en: And Saint-Just had written to Robespierre, I do not know you, but you are a great man.
sentences.zh: 圣茹斯特曾写信给罗伯斯庇尔：“我不认识你，但你是个伟人。”

sentences.en: You are not merely the deputy of a province.
sentences.zh: “你不仅仅是一个省的代表。”

sentences.en: You are the deputy of the republic and of mankind.
sentences.zh: “你是共和国和全人类的代表。”

sentences.en: And you can imagine how this goes down with Robespierre.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象罗伯斯庇尔看到这番话时的反应。

sentences.en: He thinks this is brilliant.
sentences.zh: 他觉得这简直妙极了。

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: So he and Saint-Just become very close.
sentences.zh: 所以他和圣茹斯特变得非常亲密。

sentences.en: But I think Saint-Just is actually much more intellectually formidable than Robespierre.
sentences.zh: 但我认为圣茹斯特在思想上实际上比罗伯斯庇尔更为强大。

sentences.en: And he becomes the great ideologue of the revolution at its most violent.
sentences.zh: 他成为了革命达到最暴力阶段时的伟大思想家。

sentences.en: And he will come to be given this nickname, the Archangel of Terror, which I think brilliantly conveys.
sentences.zh: 他后来被赋予了一个绰号——恐怖大天使，我认为这个绰号非常传神。

sentences.en: It's the sense of glamour that comes to attach itself to him.
sentences.zh: 这种魅力开始依附在他的身上。

sentences.en: And Saint-Just is the model for almost the kind of the Byronic terrorist that haunts the pages of Dostoevsky or people like that.
sentences.zh: 圣茹斯特几乎成为了陀思妥耶夫斯基等人的作品中那种拜伦式的恐怖主义者的原型。

sentences.en: The sense that there is a poetry in terror that risks consuming the world.
sentences.zh: 让人感到恐怖之中蕴含着一种足以吞噬世界的诗意。

sentences.en: He's like somebody from the Bader-Meinhof group or some American fringe group in the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 他就像是来自巴德尔-迈因霍夫集团或是20世纪70年代某个美国边缘组织的人。

sentences.en: Long hair.
sentences.zh: 长发。

sentences.en: He's quite cool.
sentences.zh: 他相当酷。

sentences.en: He's terrifying.
sentences.zh: 他令人畏惧。

sentences.en: He's ruthless.
sentences.zh: 他冷酷无情。

sentences.en: He's cold-blooded.
sentences.zh: 他冷血。

sentences.en: Well, he's simultaneously cold when it comes to condemning other people to death.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他在判处他人死刑时确实铁石心肠。

sentences.en: But there is something about him that gets other people very excited.
sentences.zh: 但他身上某种特质却让其他人感到无比兴奋。

sentences.en: But I think also in the 19th and then into the 20th century, what gives him this glamour is the sense that he, more than perhaps anybody else involved in the revolution,
sentences.zh: 但我也认为，在19世纪乃至20世纪，赋予他这种魅力的原因在于，与其他参与革命的人相比，他更像是……

sentences.en: is a precursor of communist revolution.
sentences.zh: 共产主义革命的先驱。

sentences.en: Yes, completely.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全如此。

sentences.en: He's an avatar of what is to come.
sentences.zh: 他是未来事物的化身。

sentences.en: So Robespierre had these two very, very charismatic allies.
sentences.zh: 所以罗伯斯庇尔拥有这两位极具个人魅力的盟友。

sentences.en: And they obviously provide him with political support on the committee.
sentences.zh: 他们在委员会里显然为他提供了政治支持。

sentences.en: Robespierre has his own sense of destiny and of self-assurance.
sentences.zh: 罗伯斯庇尔有着强烈的宿命感和自信心。

sentences.en: And so he comes to take an ever more commanding position on the committee.
sentences.zh: 因此，他在委员会中占据了越来越主导的地位。

sentences.en: And already, only a few days after he has joined the committee, an observer at one of their meetings could describe Robespierre's colleagues, and I quote,
sentences.zh: 而就在他加入委员会仅几天后，会议上的一位观察员对罗伯斯庇尔的同事们作出了这样的描述，我引述如下：

sentences.en: as silent in the face of his words and his principles.
sentences.zh: 面对他的言辞和原则，他们噤若寒蝉。

sentences.en: So these words and principles, I mean, what is he saying?
sentences.zh: 所以这些言辞和原则，我是说，他究竟在讲些什么？

sentences.en: He's talking about the people, presumably.
sentences.zh: 我想他谈论的应该正是人民。

sentences.en: He's talking about how much he believes in them.
sentences.zh: 他在谈论自己有多么深信他们。

sentences.en: He's talking about the conspiracy.
sentences.zh: 他在谈论那场阴谋。

sentences.en: But what else?
sentences.zh: 但除此之外还有什么？

sentences.en: Well, I think his fundamental principles are admirable ones.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为他的核心原则确实令人钦佩。

sentences.en: He has a firm faith in democracy and in constitutional government.
sentences.zh: 他对民主和立宪政府抱有坚定的信仰。

sentences.en: And Dominic, you mentioned very briefly in the first episode that a new constitution was being celebrated as Charlotte Corday arrived in Paris.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，你在第一集里曾简短提到过，当夏洛蒂·科黛抵达巴黎时，人们正在庆祝一项新宪法。

sentences.en: And this constitution had been drawn up by Robespierre, abetted by Saint-Just and Couton.
sentences.zh: 而这部宪法是由罗伯斯庇尔起草的，圣茹斯特和库东则从旁协助。

sentences.en: And they'd done it in record time.
sentences.zh: 他们以破纪录的速度完成了这项工作。

sentences.en: They'd drawn it up in early June.
sentences.zh: 他们在六月初就起草好了。

sentences.en: And its provisions were ones that Robespierre absolutely believed in.
sentences.zh: 其中的各项条款都是罗伯斯庇尔深信不疑的。

sentences.en: It offers a commitment to universal male suffrage without any qualification, free public education, which is to be funded by progressive taxation.
sentences.zh: 它承诺实行无任何限制的成年男子普京，以及通过累进税资助的免费公共教育。

sentences.en: And it declares as a matter of national principle that the state has a duty of care towards its most unfortunate citizens.
sentences.zh: 作为一项国家原则，它宣告国家有责任对最不幸的公民给予关怀。

sentences.en: So this is, and I don't think it's an anachronism to use this phrase, the most progressive constitution that history has ever seen up to this point.
sentences.zh: 因此，这是——我认为用这个词并不算时代错位——历史上迄今为止见过最进步的宪法。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, it's the kind of thing that progressives in any Western state today would very happily vote for, I think.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这正是当今任何西方国家的进步派都会非常乐意投票支持的那种东西。

sentences.en: And the French people themselves vote for it, don't they?
sentences.zh: 而且法国人民自己也投票支持了它，对吧？

sentences.en: They have a referendum and they, by a massive majority, they endorse it.
sentences.zh: 他们举行了全民公投，并以压倒性多数予以通过。

sentences.en: They do.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So this is held throughout June and July, and the results are announced on the 10th of August, which is the anniversary of the abolition of the monarchy.
sentences.zh: 这场公投在六月和七月举行，结果于8月10日公布，而那天正是废除君主制的周年纪念日。

sentences.en: And it turns out that almost 2 million people have voted in favour of it and only 11,600 against it.
sentences.zh: 结果显示，近两百万人投票赞成，而反对者仅有11600人。

sentences.en: And so Robespierre is delighted.
sentences.zh: 因此罗伯斯庇尔欣喜若狂。

sentences.en: It's now been proven that he is the voice of the people.
sentences.zh: 现在事实证明，他就是人民的代言人。

sentences.en: They completely back him.
sentences.zh: 他们完全支持他。

sentences.en: And since he has, you know, he essentially is the author of this constitution, of course he wants to see it put into action.
sentences.zh: 既然他，你知道的，基本上就是这部宪法的作者，他当然希望看到它付诸实施。

sentences.en: The problem is that he feels that France is not yet ready for it, not with the revolution being menaced by a conspiracy that threatens to destroy it altogether.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，他觉得法国还没准备好，因为革命正受到一场扬言将其彻底摧毁的阴谋的威胁。

sentences.en: And so he says, what we must do is first defeat the conspiracy and then introduce the constitution.
sentences.zh: 因此他说，我们必须做的是首先击败阴谋，然后再推行宪法。

sentences.en: And sure enough, in the event, so on the 10th of September, 1793, the constitution will end up being officially suspended.
sentences.zh: 果不其然，在1793年9月10日，这部宪法最终被正式搁置。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And Robespierre completely backs this.
sentences.zh: 罗伯斯庇尔对此完全支持。

sentences.en: And it's due reflection of the fact that, you know, the revolution is facing massive crisis and challenges everywhere.
sentences.zh: 这恰恰反映了一个事实：你知道的，革命正面临着无处不在的巨大危机和挑战。

sentences.en: And Robespierre feels that the focus should be not in introducing the constitution,
sentences.zh: 罗伯斯庇尔认为，当务之急不应该是推行宪法，

sentences.en: but rather on defeating this kind of hydra-headed conspiracy that is threatening to destroy it completely.
sentences.zh: 而是要击败这种正威胁要将其彻底毁灭的、多头怪兽般的阴谋。

sentences.en: But this brings us, doesn't it, Tom, to the terror, to the reign of terror.
sentences.zh: 但这就把我们带到了恐怖统治，汤姆，即恐怖时期。

sentences.en: So how to defeat the conspiracy.
sentences.zh: 也就是如何击败阴谋。

sentences.en: And his strategy here is implacable and ruthless.
sentences.zh: 他在此采取的策略冷酷无情且毫不妥协。

sentences.en: And, I mean, am I exaggerating, do you think, to describe it as he's going to mobilize all the resources of society, effectively every man, woman and child,
sentences.zh: 而且，我是说，如果我将其描述为他将动员社会的一切资源，实际上是每一个男人、女人和孩子，

sentences.en: in a kind of national effort to root out conspiracy and any deviation from the path of revolutionary righteousness.
sentences.zh: 发起一场全民运动来根除阴谋以及对革命正统道路的任何背离，这算不算夸张？

sentences.en: Well, if you were going to defeat a conspiracy that is menacing the people, you need the people in their entirety to defeat it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果你要击败一个威胁到人民的阴谋，你需要全体人民的力量来战胜它。

sentences.en: So let me read what he wrote in the catechism that he was drawing up on the evening before he joined the Committee of Public Safety.
sentences.zh: 让我来读读他在加入公共安全委员会前夕所编写的教义问答中写的内容。

sentences.en: And this is a very brutal prescription for ending the crisis.
sentences.zh: 这是一剂极其残酷的结束危机的药方。

sentences.en: So he wrote,
sentences.zh: 他是这样写的：

sentences.en: And it is very obviously one that contradicts Robespierre's deeply held and oft-expressed opposition to capital punishment.
sentences.zh: 这显然与罗伯斯庇尔根深蒂固且屡次表达的反对死刑的立场相矛盾。

sentences.en: And so listeners may be wondering, well, what impact does this have on his reputation for unyielding principle?
sentences.zh: 所以听众可能会想，这对他一贯坚持原则的名声有什么影响呢？

sentences.en: And the answer is, it has no impact whatsoever.
sentences.zh: 答案是，没有任何影响。

sentences.en: And the reason for this is that even as Robespierre has been saying he's opposed to the death penalty, he has also, right from the very beginning of the revolution back in 1789,
sentences.zh: 原因在于，尽管罗伯斯庇尔一直在说他反对死刑，但他也从1789年革命伊始的最初时刻起，

sentences.en: been arguing that to live through a revolution changes everything.
sentences.zh: 就一直在论证：经历一场革命会改变一切。

sentences.en: That there might come a time when civilized norms would need to be suspended and that the end must justify the means.
sentences.zh: 文明规范可能需要在某个时刻被暂停，而且目的必须将手段合理化。

sentences.en: And because he has been arguing this since 1789 at a time where this prescription was unthinkable to most enthusiasts for the revolution,
sentences.zh: 由于他自1789年以来就一直在这样论证——而在当时，这种做法对大多数革命狂热分子来说是不可想象的——

sentences.en: it gives him the moral authority to push this policy and not to seem like he's just kind of dreamt it up as a way of buttressing his own power.
sentences.zh: 这赋予了他推行这一政策的道德权威，使他看起来不只是为了巩固自己的权力而凭空捏造。

sentences.en: So as late as the trial of Louis XVI for which Robespierre had voted, he'd expressed his hope that Louis' execution would be the last that the revolution would require.
sentences.zh: 甚至在审判路易十六时——罗伯斯庇尔曾为此投了赞成票——他还表达过希望路易的处决将是革命所需的最后一次。

sentences.en: That there would be no need for the state to mandate the putting to death of any further person.
sentences.zh: 国家将不再需要下令剥夺任何其他人的生命。

sentences.en: But as you said in the previous episode, the thing that changes everything is the defection of Du Maurier,
sentences.zh: 但正如你在上一集所说，改变一切的事件是迪穆里埃的叛变，

sentences.en: this former Girondin minister who had won great victories for the French Republic,
sentences.zh: 这位曾为法兰西共和国赢得过伟大胜利的前吉伦特派大臣，

sentences.en: but then had kind of turned coat and gone over to the enemies of France and which had been interpreted by Robespierre as by Jacobin and Montagnard and people like that as a potentially mortal blow to the revolution.
sentences.zh: 却突然叛变投敌，投向了法国的敌人，这在罗伯斯庇尔、雅各宾派和山岳派等人眼中被视为对革命的潜在致命打击。

sentences.en: And because it's a potentially mortal blow, that means that those who are responsible for it cannot possibly be treated with mercy.
sentences.zh: 正因为这是一次潜在的致命打击，这意味着对那些负有责任的人绝不能心慈手软。

sentences.en: So to quote Robespierre, for every attempt made against the security of the state or the liberty, equality, unity and indivisibility of the Republic,
sentences.zh: 用罗伯斯庇尔的话来说，对于任何企图危害国家安全或共和国的自由、平等、统一与不可分割性的行为，

sentences.en: capital punishment is now the only appropriate punishment.
sentences.zh: 死刑现在是唯一恰当的惩罚。

sentences.en: And people understand that this goes against his opposition to capital punishment,
sentences.zh: 人们明白这违背了他对死刑的反对立场，

sentences.en: but they kind of respect the fact that he's prepared to sacrifice that principle on the much greater principle, which is that the revolution must be saved.
sentences.zh: 但他们多少尊重这样一个事实：他准备为了一个更伟大的原则——即必须拯救革命——而牺牲那个原则。

sentences.en: And so he's not seen as someone who is kind of shifting his position.
sentences.zh: 因此，他并没有被视为一个立场动摇的人。

sentences.en: He's being seen as someone who is cleaving to the ultimate needs of the revolution, even if that comes as moral cost to himself.
sentences.zh: 他被视为一个紧守革命终极需求的人，哪怕这需要付出他个人的道德代价。

sentences.en: I mean, one of the points actually is that in the next few months, he and Saint-Jus spend a lot of time making speeches to explain their rationale.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，其中一点实际上是，在接下来的几个月里，他和圣茹斯特花了很多时间发表长篇大论来解释他们的基本理据。

sentences.en: One of the points they make is that if you oppose the government, if you're undermining the national war effort, and therefore you're obviously working for the foreign conspiracy,
sentences.zh: 他们提出的其中一点是，如果你反对政府，如果你在破坏国家的战争努力，从而显然是在为外国阴谋效力，

sentences.en: you don't really count as a citizen, because true citizens would be with us.
sentences.zh: 你就根本算不上是一个公民，因为真正的公民会与我们站在一起。

sentences.en: And if you are not a citizen, then all our talk of, despite their idea that the human rights stuff is universal, they sort of have their cake and eat it.
sentences.zh: 如果你不是公民，那么我们谈论的那些——尽管他们认为人权是普遍的，但他们有点像是在鱼与熊掌兼得。

sentences.en: Because they say, if you're not a citizen and you're a foreign traitor, then all the right stuff doesn't apply to you.
sentences.zh: 因为他们说，如果你不是公民而是外国叛徒，那么所有关于权利的东西都不适用于你。

sentences.en: You don't have any rights under the law, so we can do whatever we want to you.
sentences.zh: 你在法律下没有任何权利，所以我们可以对你为所欲为。

sentences.en: This citizenship depends on, as it were, political correctness.
sentences.zh: 这种公民身份可以说是取决于所谓的政治正确。

sentences.en: Well, virtue, I think, they do explicitly say that kind of virtue without teeth is worth nothing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，至于美德，我认为他们确实明确说过，那种没有牙齿的美德一文不值。

sentences.en: Of course, yes.
sentences.zh: 当然，是的。

sentences.en: And that therefore, terror is a manifestation of virtue.
sentences.zh: 因此，恐怖正是美德的一种表现。

sentences.en: I mean, we'll probably come to this when we look at what happens with Danton.
sentences.zh: 我们讲到丹东的遭遇时可能会再谈到这一点。

sentences.en: But this idea that terror is a manifestation of virtue, this is a principle that is starting to evolve across the summer of 1793.
sentences.zh: 但恐怖是美德的表现这一观点，正是1793年夏天开始演变的一项原则。

sentences.en: And interestingly, its initial focus is in the field of military affairs, which is absolutely not Robespierre's vibe at all.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，它最初的焦点是在军事事务领域，这与罗伯斯庇尔的风格完全背道而驰。

sentences.en: I mean, he has no experience of military matters whatsoever.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他没有任何军事事务的经验。

sentences.en: But he supports the sending on the 4th of August of twin armies to crush insurrections in the two key counter-revolutionary outbreaks, one in Lyon, one in Marseille.
sentences.zh: 但他支持在8月4日派遣两支军队去平定两个关键反革命爆发点的暴动，一个在里昂，一个在马赛。

sentences.en: And Lyon is invested on the 7th of August, and the siege of that city will drag on for months.
sentences.zh: 里昂在8月7日被包围，对该城的围攻将持续数月之久。

sentences.en: But Marseille is reduced to obedience very rapidly.
sentences.zh: 但马赛很快就被迫屈服了。

sentences.en: So it's occupied on the 25th of August, and there are mass reprisals.
sentences.zh: 因此它在8月25日被攻占，并发生了大规模的报复行动。

sentences.en: And Marseille itself loses its name, and it's kind of renamed Ville-s-en-Norme, so kind of the town without a name.
sentences.zh: 马赛本身甚至失去了自己的名字，被改名为“无名之城”（Ville-sans-nom）。

sentences.en: And two days before Marseille capitulates to the forces of the revolution, the National Convention had taken a massive, massive step,
sentences.zh: 就在马赛向革命军队投降的两天前，国民公会采取了一个极其重大的步骤，

sentences.en: a step that will resonate not just through the history of the revolution, but through the entire future of industrial warfare.
sentences.zh: 这个步骤不仅在革命史中产生共鸣，也将对整个工业化战争的未来产生深远影响。

sentences.en: They enact a levee en masse.
sentences.zh: 他们颁布了大规模征兵令（levee en masse）。

sentences.en: So this is the first mass conscription of the modern age, and its prescription, I mean,
sentences.zh: 这是现代史上的第一次全民总动员，而它的条款，我的意思是，

sentences.en: is people who have read about the war efforts of the competence in the First or Second World Wars will recognise this.
sentences.zh: 读过一战或二战中各参战国战争努力的人都会对此感到熟悉。

sentences.en: So it says,
sentences.zh: 它是这样说的：

sentences.en: So it is a seismic moment for the first time, an entire nation is being summoned to arMs.
sentences.zh: 因此这是一个震撼人心的时刻，整个国家历史上第一次被召唤拿起武器。

sentences.en: And in the long run, this levee en masse will make France effectively invincible in battle for decades,
sentences.zh: 从长远来看，这起全民征兵将使法国在未来几十年的战斗中几乎所向披靡，

sentences.en: because France has by far the largest reserves of manpower of any country in Europe.
sentences.zh: 因为法国拥有欧洲任何国家都望尘莫及的最大兵源储备。

sentences.en: And so by summoning it to arms, it makes itself completely irresistible in battle.
sentences.zh: 因此，通过武装全国，它在战斗中变得完全不可阻挡。

sentences.en: This is the bedrock, the foundation stone in the Napoleonic Empire.
sentences.zh: 这是拿破仑帝国的基石。

sentences.en: Yes, it is.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: But the immediate circumstances in which this levee is summoned, it's not at all obvious that this policy is going to work.
sentences.zh: 但在这项征兵令下达的即时环境下，这项政策是否行得通还完全是个未知数。

sentences.en: So as August turns to September in 1793, things in Paris are becoming very grim.
sentences.zh: 因此，随着1793年8月转入9月，巴黎的局势变得非常严峻。

sentences.en: There's no bread.
sentences.zh: 买不到面包。

sentences.en: Inflation is going through the roof.
sentences.zh: 通货膨胀率直冲云霄。

sentences.en: Even Roespierre can't afford to buy his beloved silk stockings.
sentences.zh: 甚至连罗伯斯庇尔也买不起他心爱的丝绸长袜了。

sentences.en: So you know that things are getting very bad.
sentences.zh: 所以你知道情况已经变得多么糟糕。

sentences.en: And then on the 2nd of September comes completely devastating news.
sentences.zh: 接着在9月2日，传来了完全毁灭性的消息。

sentences.en: And this is news from Toulon, the great naval base on the south coaSt.
sentences.zh: 这是来自南部海岸伟大海军基地土伦的消息。

sentences.en: And this is that the counter-revolutionaries surrendered the great port to the British.
sentences.zh: 消息称反革命分子将这座伟大的港口交给了英国人。

sentences.en: Of all people.
sentences.zh: 偏偏是他们。

sentences.en: So we talked about this in our series on Nelson, and we saw it from the British perspective.
sentences.zh: 我们在关于纳尔逊的系列节目中讨论过此事，当时我们是从英国人的视角来看待的。

sentences.en: But from the French perspective, the loss of this key naval base, traitors have betrayed it to the Royal Navy of all forces.
sentences.zh: 但从法国的角度来看，失去这个关键海军基地——叛徒竟然把它出卖给了英国皇家海军，

sentences.en: It's completely devastating.
sentences.zh: 这简直是毁灭性的打击。

sentences.en: And so unsurprisingly in Paris, there is a massive new wave of paranoia.
sentences.zh: 因此不出所料，巴黎掀起了一股巨大无比的新多疑热潮。

sentences.en: And starving mobs take to the streets, the enraged, you talked about in the previous episode, the enraged.
sentences.zh: 忍饥挨饿的暴民走上街头，也就是你在上一集里提到过的“忿激派”（The Enraged）。

sentences.en: Oh yeah, moustaches.
sentences.zh: 哦对，大胡子们。

sentences.en: People with their bristling moustaches, terrifying.
sentences.zh: 留着竖起胡须的人，太吓人了。

sentences.en: And one of their particular leaders, who is a seasoned radical named Gaspard Chaumet, he puts into words their motivation in a great public speech.
sentences.zh: 他们的其中一位领袖，一位经验丰富的激进分子名叫加斯帕尔·肖梅特（Gaspard Chaumet），在一场大型公众演讲中用言语表达了他们的动机。

sentences.en: Every day we learn of new trees and new crimes.
sentences.zh: 我们每天都能听到新的背叛和新的罪行。

sentences.en: Every day we discover the emergence of new plots.
sentences.zh: 我们每天都发现新的阴谋正在浮出水面。

sentences.en: And these words carry massive weight with the sans-culottes and the enraged, because Chaumet is not some nobody from the sluMs.
sentences.zh: 这些话在无套裤汉和忿激派中产生了巨大的分量，因为肖梅特并非贫民窟里无足轻重的小人物。

sentences.en: He is effectively the chief legal and administrative officer in the Paris Commune, which is basically the municipal government of the capital.
sentences.zh: 他实际上是巴黎公社的首席法律和行政官员，而公社基本上就是首都的市政政府。

sentences.en: And on the 5th of September, Chaumet leads a march on the convention.
sentences.zh: 9月5日，肖梅特率领游行队伍前往国民公会。

sentences.en: So this is the day after he'd given that rabble-rousing speech.
sentences.zh: 这就是他在发表了那番煽动性演讲的第二天。

sentences.en: And a great crowd of moustachioed enraged follow him, cheering, singing patriotic songs, waving slogans and banners, war on tyrants, war on aristocrats, all of that.
sentences.zh: 一大群留着胡须的忿激派紧随其后，欢呼着，唱着爱国歌曲，挥舞着标语和横幅：对暴君开战，对贵族开战，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And they arrive in the convention, and Chaumet leads them on a kind of invasion of the convention.
sentences.zh: 他们抵达国民公会，肖梅特带领他们某种程度上“入侵”了公会。

sentences.en: And inside he delivers a petition on behalf of the demonstrators who are massed at his back.
sentences.zh: 在里面，他代表集结在他身后的示威者递交了一份请愿书。

sentences.en: And then he gives a lengthy speech.
sentences.zh: 随后他发表了一场长篇演讲。

sentences.en: And when he finishes this speech, upstands Barrère, and he gives that momentous slogan with which we began this episode, let terror be the order of the day.
sentences.zh: 当他结束演讲时，巴雷尔（Barrère）站了起来，发表了我们在本集开头提到的那个重磅口号：让恐怖成为当下的秩序。

sentences.en: And Barrère goes on to say, let us be in revolution because everywhere counter-revolution is being woven by our enemies.
sentences.zh: 巴雷尔接着说，让我们处于革命状态吧，因为反革命正在被我们的敌人四处密谋编织。

sentences.en: The blade of the law should hover over all the guilty.
sentences.zh: 法律的利剑应当高悬于所有罪犯头顶。

sentences.en: Now, Robespierre, he is president of the convention at the time.
sentences.zh: 当时，罗伯斯庇尔正担任国民公会主席。

sentences.en: He actually finds the invasion of the petitioners unsettling rather than inspiring.
sentences.zh: 实际上，他发现请愿者的这种侵入与其说是鼓舞人心，不如说是令人不安。

sentences.en: You know, he's a stickler for propriety.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他是个拘泥于礼节的人。

sentences.en: He doesn't really approve of this action from the streets.
sentences.zh: 他其实并不赞成这种来自街头的行动。

sentences.en: But with his kind of customary acuity, he's very quick to take advantage of this proclamation that terror should be the order of the day.
sentences.zh: 但凭借他惯有的敏锐，他非常迅速地利用了“恐怖应当成为当下的秩序”这一宣告。

sentences.en: As we said, it doesn't become an official motion of the convention, but it's taken on board by the committee.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所说，它并未成为国民公会的正式动议，但已被委员会采纳。

sentences.en: And isn't this just a brilliant example of the way in which rather than necessarily the whole business being directed from the top, there are radical images from the streets.
sentences.zh: 这难道不是一个绝佳的例子吗：比起一切事务都必须由高层指挥，街头往往先涌现出激进的呼声。

sentences.en: And part of the process of institutionalizing the terror is actually saying, well, we don't want mobs roaming around the streets, lynching people and stuff.
sentences.zh: 而将恐怖制度化的部分过程，实际上就是说，嗯，我们不希望暴民在街上游荡、私刑处决他人之类的事情。

sentences.en: We want to centralize it, bureaucratize it.
sentences.zh: 我们要把它集中化、官僚化。

sentences.en: We want it done on a proper basis.
sentences.zh: 我们希望在适当的基础上完成它。

sentences.en: And that's what Robespierre and the Committee of Public Safety are really all about.
sentences.zh: 这正是罗伯斯庇尔和公共安全委员会真正关心的核心。

sentences.en: Yeah, they're saying, OK, you want terror and we agree.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们是在说，好吧，你们想要恐怖，我们同意。

sentences.en: The needs of the republic demand it.
sentences.zh: 共和国的需求需要它。

sentences.en: Let's provide the legal instruments that will enable us to enforce it.
sentences.zh: 让我们提供能够让我们执行它的法律工具吧。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Rather than having mobs going around murdering people in prisons.
sentences.zh: 而不是让暴民四处在监狱里谋杀囚犯。

sentences.en: That's basically it.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是这样。

sentences.en: That's that's their kind of rationale.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们的某种理论依据。

sentences.en: And I think, you know, one shouldn't be cynical about it.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，你知道的，人们不应该对此持冷嘲热讽的态度。

sentences.en: They think that this is for the best, I think.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这才是最好的选择，我是这么想的。

sentences.en: So what does this mean in practice?
sentences.zh: 所以这在实践中意味着什么？

sentences.en: So on the 5th of September, they split up the Revolutionary Tribunal, which had been established a few months previously to try political prisoners.
sentences.zh: 于是在9月5日，他们将几个月前为审判政治犯而设立的革命法庭拆分了。

sentences.en: They split it into four concurrent chambers, which means that they can expedite the processing of of cases.
sentences.zh: 他们把它拆分成了四个同时运作的审判庭，这意味着他们可以加快案件的处理进度。

sentences.en: They decree that the judges and jurors who are trying these cases should be appointed by the committee themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们下令，审理这些案件的法官和陪审团成员应由委员会亲自任命。

sentences.en: So that means that they can vet who's going to be on these juries.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他们可以审查谁将进入这些陪审团。

sentences.en: And following this, unsurprisingly, the acquittal rate drops precipitously.
sentences.zh: 随之而来的是，不出所料，无罪释放率急剧下降。

sentences.en: So it increasingly becomes very unusual to be acquitted.
sentences.zh: 因此，被判无罪变得越来越罕见。

sentences.en: And then on the 17th of September, the key development, the law of suspects, it's called.
sentences.zh: 然后在9月17日，关键进展来了，被称为“嫌疑犯法”。

sentences.en: Very notorious process of legislation because it vastly broadens the category of person who is liable for arreSt.
sentences.zh: 这是一个臭名昭著的立法进程，因为它极大地扩大了可能被捕的人的范围。

sentences.en: So just to go through people who can now be arraigned under this law of suspects, nobles who had displayed a lack of patriotism and revolutionary zeal.
sentences.zh: 因此，仅举出根据这项“嫌疑犯法”现在可以传讯的人，那些表现出缺乏爱国主义和革命热情的贵族。

sentences.en: Emigre, so people who had fled abroad and government employees who have been discharged from office.
sentences.zh: 流亡者，也就是逃往国外的人，以及被罢免的政府雇员。

sentences.en: And so there are quite a few of those.
sentences.zh: 所以这类人相当多。

sentences.en: Anyone who lacks a certificate of good citizenship.
sentences.zh: 任何缺乏良好公民证书的人。

sentences.en: And this certificate was something that is issued by the revolutionary authorities to serve as an identity card.
sentences.zh: 而这张证书是革命当局颁发的，用作身份证件。

sentences.en: But inevitably, it has come to serve as well as a kind of an official stamp of ideological purity.
sentences.zh: 但不可避免的是，它也开始充当一种意识形态纯洁性的官方印章。

sentences.en: If you don't have one, then you are, by definition, a counter-revolutionary.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有一张，那么根据定义，你就是反革命分子。

sentences.en: So you need one.
sentences.zh: 所以你需要一张。

sentences.en: Anyone who fails to demonstrate a satisfactory discharge of their civic duties.
sentences.zh: 任何未能证明圆满履行公民职责的人。

sentences.en: I mean, again, if you want to get rid of someone, you could apply that to almost anyone.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，同样，如果你想除掉某人，你可以把这条套用到几乎任何人身上。

sentences.en: And then most sweepingly of all, and I quote, those who by their conduct, relations or language spoken or written have shown themselves partisans of tyranny.
sentences.zh: 然后是最具包罗万象的一条，我引用原话：“凡是其行为、交往、所说或所写语言显示自己是暴政党羽的人。”

sentences.en: So this is a sweeping, I mean, literally terrifying law.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一条包罗万象的，我的意思是，字面意义上令人毛骨悚然的法律。

sentences.en: But of course, for true patriots, that's the point of it.
sentences.zh: 但当然，对于真正的爱国者来说，这就是它的意义所在。

sentences.en: That's what it's serving.
sentences.zh: 这就是它所起到的作用。

sentences.en: And Tackett draws on the diaries of this woman, Rosalie Julien, who's the mother of one of Robespierre's agents out in the provinces.
sentences.zh: 塔凯特借鉴了这个名叫罗莎莉·朱利安的女性的日记，她是罗伯斯庇尔在各省的特务之一的母亲。

sentences.en: And she thinks the law of suspects is brilliant.
sentences.zh: 她认为“嫌疑犯法”棒极了。

sentences.en: She absolutely loves it.
sentences.zh: 她绝对爱死它了。

sentences.en: And she writes to one of her sons, It is so necessary for the security of the state that even those who are innocent victims cannot complain if they are truly Republican.
sentences.zh: 她写信给她的一个儿子：“它对国家安全是如此必要，以至于即使是无辜的牺牲品，如果是真正的共和党人，也不能抱怨。”

sentences.en: So in other words, you know, you get convicted, sent to the guillotine.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，你知道的，你被定罪，送上断头台。

sentences.en: You shouldn't moan about it, but just reflect that you're serving the cause of the people.
sentences.zh: 你不应该为此抱怨，而应该反思你正在为人民的事业服务。

sentences.en: We've heard this so many times in history in similar circumstances.
sentences.zh: 我们在历史上的相似情况下听过太多次这样的话了。

sentences.en: You know, if you are innocent, you have nothing to fear.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果你是无辜的，你没什么好害怕的。

sentences.en: So, and if you have something to fear, if you're frightened, well, that just shows you're guilty.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你有什么好怕的，如果你感到害怕，好吧，那恰恰说明你有罪。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, I think that reflects the mood of, you know, complete paranoia that is governing not just the committee itself, not just the convention, but the streets of Paris.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为这反映了一种情绪，你知道的，即完全的偏执狂，它不仅统治着委员会本身，不仅统治着国民公会，还统治着巴黎的街道。

sentences.en: There's a sense that there are traitors and conspirators everywhere and that it's only by really violent repression that the revolution can be saved.
sentences.zh: 有一种感觉，即叛国者和阴谋家无处不在，只有通过极其暴力的镇压才能拯救革命。

sentences.en: And again, I mean, anyone who has seen the operations of social media today will kind of recognise a very pale echo of that mood, I think.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，我的意思是，任何看过今天社交媒体运作方式的人都会认出那种情绪的一个非常苍白的迴响，我认为。

sentences.en: When the mob moves, the mob moves.
sentences.zh: 当暴民行动时，暴民就是会行动。

sentences.en: If you have been cancelled, it just shows that you were right to be cancelled in the first place.
sentences.zh: 如果你被“取消”了，这恰恰说明你当初被“取消”是正确的。

sentences.en: But you know what?
sentences.zh: 但你知道吗？

sentences.en: The thing is, it works.
sentences.zh: 关键是，它管用。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The revolution is saved.
sentences.zh: 革命得救了。

sentences.en: The terror serves the purpose for which it has been introduced.
sentences.zh: 恐怖达到了它被引入的目的。

sentences.en: A key moment comes on the 6th of October when Lyon, the second city of France, it's been under siege for two months.
sentences.zh: 一个关键时刻出现在10月6日，当时法国第二大城市里昂已经被围困了两个月。

sentences.en: It finally falls.
sentences.zh: 它最终陷落了。

sentences.en: And the Committee of Public Safety decree mass executions and the destruction of all the buildings in the city that are not owned by the people.
sentences.zh: 公共安全委员会下令进行大规模处决，并摧毁城中所有不属于人民的建筑物。

sentences.en: And Robespierre, echoing a line in Tacitus, declares epigrammatically, Lyon is no more.
sentences.zh: 罗伯斯庇尔呼应了塔西陀的一句话，精辟地宣称：“里昂不复存在了。”

sentences.en: And Couton, so the guy who had too much sex and got confined to a wheelchair as a result, and he's the committee's man on the scene.
sentences.zh: 而库东，那个因为性生活过多导致结果被禁锢在轮椅上的人，他是委员会在现场的人。

sentences.en: He wants to go even further and deport vast swathes of the population, which he sees as kind of incorrigibly counter-revolutionary.
sentences.zh: 他想走得更远，把大片人口流放，在他看来，这些人是某种不可救药的反革命分子。

sentences.en: And he writes to Robespierre and says, you know, they're so counter-revolutionary that I feel they will be for generations.
sentences.zh: 他写信给罗伯斯庇尔说，你知道的，他们是如此反革命，以至于我觉得他们世世代代都会如此。

sentences.en: So we need to bust them out and kind of settle them in the depths of the country.
sentences.zh: 所以我们需要把他们赶出去，把他们安置在国家的腹地。

sentences.en: But Robespierre refuses this.
sentences.zh: 但罗伯斯庇尔拒绝了这一点。

sentences.en: He says that's too extreme.
sentences.zh: 他说这太极端了。

sentences.en: And he continues to insist that the mass of the people are naturally virtuous.
sentences.zh: 他继续坚称广大民众天生是善良的。

sentences.en: They're naturally good.
sentences.zh: 他们天生是好的。

sentences.en: So even in Lyon, they can be trusted.
sentences.zh: 所以即使在里昂，他们也是可以被信任的。

sentences.en: But the people who cannot be trusted are the counter-revolutionaries who had brought Lyon to such ruin.
sentences.zh: 但是不可信任的人是那些把里昂带入如此毁灭境地的反革命分子。

sentences.en: They have to be dealt with, with extreme prejudice.
sentences.zh: 必须毫不留情地对付他们。

sentences.en: And Robespierre knows precisely who ultimately are to blame.
sentences.zh: 罗伯斯庇尔确切地知道最终应该怪谁。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So this brings us to the people that were beginning to be locked up in the last episode.
sentences.zh: 所以这把我们带到了上一集中开始被关起来的人身上。

sentences.en: And these are the people who were previously the dominant faction in the National Convention.
sentences.zh: 这些人正是之前在国民公会中占主导地位的派别。

sentences.en: And these are the Girondins.
sentences.zh: 这些就是吉伦特派。

sentences.en: Now, if you were being more critical of Robespierre, you would say, these are people with whom he once broke bread.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你对罗伯斯庇尔采取更多的批判态度，你就会说，这些人是他曾经与之共分面包的人。

sentences.en: These are people who were once members of the same radical clubs as he was.
sentences.zh: 这些人曾和他一样是同一个激进俱乐部的成员。

sentences.en: They were part of the revolution.
sentences.zh: 他们是革命的一部分。

sentences.en: They were just as enthusiastic as he was.
sentences.zh: 他们和当时的他一样充满热情。

sentences.en: But he doesn't see it that way, does he?
sentences.zh: 但他不这么看，不是吗？

sentences.en: And he has this long charge sheet that, as he sees it, leaves no room for doubt that they have actually been plotting to undermine France and its people from the very beginning.
sentences.zh: 他有一长串罪状，在他看来，这毫无疑问地表明，他们从一开始就一直在策划破坏法国及其人民。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I think this charge sheet does matter to the sense of Robespierre as someone who's personally virtuous, because even though he has broken bread with a lot of the Girondins,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这份罪状对于罗伯斯庇尔作为一个人格正直的人的形象确实很重要，因为尽管他曾与许多吉伦特派共分面包，

sentences.en: he has also been pursuing a venomous personal feud with the leader of the Girondins, Brissot, the anti-slavery campaigner, who's often seen as their leader.
sentences.zh: 但他同时也一直在与吉伦特派的领袖布里索——那个反奴隶制活动家、常被视为他们领袖的人——进行一场刻薄的个人宿怨。

sentences.en: And so it is important to Robespierre that he lays out the charge sheet so that people won't say, you know, he's just engaged in a faction battle.
sentences.zh: 因此，对罗伯斯庇尔来说，列出罪状是很重要的，这样人们就不会说，你知道的，他只是卷入了派系斗争。

sentences.en: So the charge sheet is that they had foisted this disastrous war on France.
sentences.zh: 所以罪状是，他们将这场灾难性的战争强加给了法国。

sentences.en: It was a Girondin who had pushed France into declaring war on Prussia and Austria.
sentences.zh: 正是吉伦特派将法国推向了对普鲁士和奥地利宣战。

sentences.en: And then in the form of General du Maurier had tried to betray it.
sentences.zh: 然后以迪穆里埃将军的形式试图背叛它。

sentences.en: So the evidence there to Robespierre seems clear.
sentences.zh: 所以在罗伯斯庇尔看来，那里的证据很清楚。

sentences.en: The treason is arrant.
sentences.zh: 叛国行为昭然若揭。

sentences.en: He charges them with being soft on nobles, soft on priests, and that their laxness had served to foster the rebellion in the Vendée.
sentences.zh: 他指控他们对贵族心慈手软，对神职人员心慈手软，他们的松懈助长了旺代地区的叛乱。

sentences.en: He then charges that following their expulsion from the convention in June 1793, which we talked about in the previous episode, their crimes had become even more palpable.
sentences.zh: 他接着指控，在他们于1793年6月被驱逐出国民公会之后（我们在上一集中讨论过），他们的罪行变得更加明显。

sentences.en: That those who had escaped house arrest, and among these was Jean-Marie Roland, husband of Madame Roland, the Salonista, former minister of the interior under Louis XVI,
sentences.zh: 那些逃脱软禁的人，其中有让-马里·罗兰，他是沙龙女主人罗兰夫人的丈夫，路易十六时期的前内政大臣，

sentences.en: that they had all fanned out into the provinces, and that these were the traitors who had fomented the counter-revolutionary movements in Lyon, in Marseille, in Caen, in Bordeaux.
sentences.zh: 他们都散布到各省，正是这些叛徒煽动了里昂、马赛、卡昂、波尔多的反革命运动。

sentences.en: That these were the traitors who had handed Toulon over to the Royal Navy.
sentences.zh: 正是这些叛徒把土伦交给了英国皇家海军。

sentences.en: And that therefore only one punishment could possibly suffice for this abominable behavior.
sentences.zh: 因此，对于这种令人发指的行为，只有一种惩罚才可能足够。

sentences.en: And Robespierre is determined to see it enforced.
sentences.zh: 罗伯斯庇尔决心看到它被执行。

sentences.en: And I think that even though Robespierre does have this kind of personal feud with Brissot and some of the other Girondins,
sentences.zh: 并且我认为，尽管罗伯斯庇尔对布里索和其他一些吉伦特派确实有这种个人宿怨，

sentences.en: he genuinely does not see himself as governed by selfish emotions.
sentences.zh: 但他真心不认为自己是受自私情绪支配的。

sentences.en: He genuinely sees himself as Cicero foiling the conspiracy of Catiline.
sentences.zh: 他真心把自己看作是粉碎卡蒂林阴谋的西塞罗。

sentences.en: He sees himself as the disinterested defender of the people of the revolution of France.
sentences.zh: 他把自己看作是人民、法国革命的无私捍卫者。

sentences.en: And the measure of this, I think, is that enormous numbers of people agree with him.
sentences.zh: 我认为，这可以通过大量的人同意他的看法来衡量。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: They agree with his self-estimation.
sentences.zh: 他们同意他对自己的估价。

sentences.en: And people in the committee, people in the convention.
sentences.zh: 委员会里的人，国民公会里的人。

sentences.en: Yeah, they do.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们确实同意。

sentences.en: They compete and they back him.
sentences.zh: 他们竞争并支持他。

sentences.en: And so because of this, he is able to nail the Girondins as the people who have to be punished for all the disasters that are overwhelming France.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，他能够将吉伦特派钉死为必须为压垮法国的所有灾难承担责任的罪人。

sentences.en: And so those Girondins leaders who are still at liberty are declared outlaws.
sentences.zh: 因此，那些仍然自由的吉伦特派领袖被宣布为不受法律保护的人。

sentences.en: And when they're caught, they are guillotined.
sentences.zh: 当他们被抓住时，就会被送上断头台。

sentences.en: And some of them commit suicide.
sentences.zh: 其中一些人自杀身亡。

sentences.en: And so there's kind of terrible story of two prominent Girondins who commit suicide out in the countryside in a field.
sentences.zh: 因此有一个可怕的故事，关于两个杰出的吉伦特派在乡下的田野里自杀。

sentences.en: And their bodies are found a week later, half devoured by wolves.
sentences.zh: 一周后他们的尸体被发现，已被狼群啃食了一半。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, in Paris, the trial opens on the 24th of October of Brissot and 20 other Girondins.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，在巴黎，10月24日，对布里索和其他20名吉伦特派的审判开始了。

sentences.en: And initially, from Robespierre's point of view, their trial does not go well.
sentences.zh: 起初，从罗伯斯庇尔的角度来看，他们的审判进展并不顺利。

sentences.en: So the accused, unsurprisingly, are very defiant.
sentences.zh: 因此，被告们毫不意外地表现得非常抗拒。

sentences.en: They're very eloquent.
sentences.zh: 他们非常能言善辩。

sentences.en: They sound convincingly patriotic because, of course, they are patriotic.
sentences.zh: 他们听起来具有说服力地爱国，因为当然，他们确实是爱国的。

sentences.en: And actually, it goes so badly for Robespierre that five days into the trial, someone in the committee stands up and proposes that the trial be abandoned,
sentences.zh: 事实上，这对罗伯斯庇尔来说是如此不利，以至于审判进行了五天后，委员会中的某个人站起来提议放弃审判，

sentences.en: that it's clearly not justified or required.
sentences.zh: 认为这显然是不合理或不需要的。

sentences.en: But Robespierre is having none of this and he steps up to the tribunal and he makes a really striking and, I think, sinister counterproposal, namely that the jury should be asked,
sentences.zh: 但罗伯斯庇尔根本不吃这一套，他走上法庭，提出了一个非常引人注目且我认为不祥的反建议，即要求陪审团回答：

sentences.en: and I quote, whether they have enough evidence to satisfy their conscience.
sentences.zh: 我引用原话：“他们是否有足够的证据来满足他们的良心。”

sentences.en: And this is massively to move the goalposts, because basically what that means is that jurors are being asked to arrive at their verdict based not on evidence.
sentences.zh: 这大大移动了球门，因为基本上这意味着陪审团被要求根据的不是证据来得出裁决。

sentences.en: That might have satisfied a traditional court of law, but rather on their own intuition, their own gut feeling,
sentences.zh: 那或许能满足一个传统的法庭，而是根据他们自己的直觉，他们自己的本能感觉，

sentences.en: their sense of whether the people who are being prosecuted are guilty or not.
sentences.zh: 他们对正在受审的人是否有罪的感觉。

sentences.en: And that's adequate.
sentences.zh: 这就足够了。

sentences.en: And this idea that you start a trial, it doesn't go well.
sentences.zh: 这种想法是，你开始一场审判，进展不顺利。

sentences.en: So you then change the rules halfway through to rig it so that it will go as you want.
sentences.zh: 于是你在中途改变规则来操纵它，好让它按你的意愿进行。

sentences.en: And we will see this again in this series, actually.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们在这个系列中还会看到这一点。

sentences.en: It's a disturbing development.
sentences.zh: 这是一个令人不安的发展。

sentences.en: And yes, at the same time, Robespierre is always anxious to give it the pattern of legality, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 是的，与此同时，罗伯斯庇尔总是渴望赋予它合法性的外衣，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, I genuinely think he feels it's the right thing to do.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我真心认为他觉得这是正确的事情要做。

sentences.en: If you're a revolutionary, he was right to do it, I think, is his feeling and the feeling of his supporters.
sentences.zh: 如果你是一个革命者，他觉得这样做是正确的，这是他和他的支持者的感觉。

sentences.en: So unsurprisingly, in the wake of all this, the Girondins accused are found guilty and the verdict is brought in on the 31st of October.
sentences.zh: 因此，不出所料，在这这一切之后，被指控的吉伦特派被判有罪，裁决于10月31日宣判。

sentences.en: And one of the 21 Girondins who've been found guilty, the moment the verdict is announced,
sentences.zh: 在被判有罪的21名吉伦特派成员中，有一人在裁决宣布的那一刻，

sentences.en: he reaches for a knife that he had smuggled into the trial and he stabs himself and kills himself.
sentences.zh: 伸手去拿一把他偷运进审判室的刀，刺伤了自己并自杀了。

sentences.en: And his corpse is still loaded onto the tumbril, together with the 20 Girondins who have neglected to commit suicide in this way.
sentences.zh: 他的尸体仍然被装上囚车，与另外20名没有以这种方式自杀的吉伦特派一起。

sentences.en: And on the way to the guillotine, the surviving 20 Girondins all sing the Marseillais.
sentences.zh: 在去断头台的路上，幸存的20名吉伦特派齐声高唱《马赛曲》。

sentences.en: And it's, you know, if you're a Girondin, it's a very stirring scene, but it doesn't help them.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果你是一个吉伦特派，这是一个非常感人的场景，但它对他们毫无帮助。

sentences.en: They will lose their heads.
sentences.zh: 他们将失去脑袋。

sentences.en: And then soon afterwards, on the 8th of November, they are followed by the most famous female Girondin.
sentences.zh: 然后不久之后，在11月8日，他们迎来了最著名的女性吉伦特派。

sentences.en: And this, of course, is the wife of Roland, Madame Roland.
sentences.zh: 当然，这就是罗兰的妻子，罗兰夫人。

sentences.en: And she is very much a living reminder of happier times when her salon had been the most fashionable, the most influential in the whole of revolutionary Paris.
sentences.zh: 她非常生动地让人想起更快乐的时光，当时她的沙龙曾是整个革命巴黎最时尚、最有影响力的沙龙。

sentences.en: The great meeting place for the Girondins throughout 1791 and 1792.
sentences.zh: 1791年和1792年吉伦特派的伟大聚会场所。

sentences.en: But not just the Girondins, because Robespierre himself had attended it.
sentences.zh: 不仅是吉伦特派，因为罗伯斯庇尔本人也曾出席过。

sentences.en: And indeed, Madame Roland had praised Robespierre two years before her execution for ranking among the small number of courageous men who are always faithful to their purpose.
sentences.zh: 事实上，罗兰夫人在她被处决前两年曾称赞罗伯斯庇尔，称他跻身于少数始终忠于其目标勇敢的人之列。

sentences.en: Robespierre, of course, would say that he's still being faithful to his purpose.
sentences.zh: 当然，罗伯斯庇尔会说他依然忠于自己的目标。

sentences.en: The irony.
sentences.zh: 多么讽刺。

sentences.en: Madame Roland, however, does not, because when she's brought to the guillotine,
sentences.zh: 然而，罗兰夫人却没有这么说，当她被带到断头台时，

sentences.en: she gazes across the square and she sees this great plinth on which there had previously stood a statue of Louis XIV.
sentences.zh: 她凝视着广场对面，看到了那个巨大的柱基，上面以前曾立着路易十四的雕像。

sentences.en: And that, of course, has been toppled and in its place has been erected a clay statue portraying liberty.
sentences.zh: 当然，那座雕像已经被推翻了，取而代之的是一座描绘自由的泥塑雕像。

sentences.en: And Madame Roland gazes at this and then utters very famous words, liberty, what crimes are committed in your name?
sentences.zh: 罗兰夫人凝视着这个，然后说出了那句非常著名的话：“自由，多少罪恶假汝之名以行！”

sentences.en: And a few days later, news of his wife death is brought to Roland and he leaves the place where he's been hiding out.
sentences.zh: 几天后，他妻子死讯传到了罗兰那里，他离开了藏身的地方。

sentences.en: And he goes out into the countryside and he sits beneath a tree on a country lane and draws out his sword stick and he impales himself.
sentences.zh: 他走到乡村，坐在一条乡村小道的一棵树下，拔出他的剑杖，刺穿了自己。

sentences.en: Now, that is the end of him.
sentences.zh: 现在，这就是他的结局。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But Dominic, Madame Roland, although her fate is famous, her last words are very famous, she's not the most famous woman,
sentences.zh: 但是多米尼克，罗兰夫人，尽管她的命运很有名，她的遗言非常有名，但她并不是最著名的女性，

sentences.en: nor even perhaps the most tragic to have perished in that autumn of 1793.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能也不是那个在1793年那个秋天陨落的最悲惨的女性。

sentences.en: Because a month earlier, a woman whom Madame Roland had always hated and despised had gone to the guillotine ahead of her.
sentences.zh: 因为在一个月前，一个罗兰夫人一直恨之入骨的女人在她之前走上了断头台。

sentences.en: And this was a woman who, for patriots everywhere, had come to seem the embodiment of everything that they were pledged to destroy.
sentences.zh: 而这个女人，对各地的爱国者来说，已经成了他们誓言摧毁的一切的化身。

sentences.en: And that woman was, of course, Marie Antoinette.
sentences.zh: 那个女人当然就是玛丽·安托瓦内特。

sentences.en: Crikey.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: So, in our next episode, we will be tracing how the revolutionaries seek to complete the final eradication of the last relics of monarchy.
sentences.zh: 所以，在我们的下一集中，我们将追溯革命者如何寻求彻底根除君主制的最后遗迹。

sentences.en: They'll destroy the symbols of monarchy.
sentences.zh: 他们将摧毁君主制的象征。

sentences.en: They will take Marie Antoinette herself to the guillotine.
sentences.zh: 他们将把玛丽·安托瓦内特本人送上断头台。

sentences.en: And we'll be talking about one of the most affecting stories of the entire revolution.
sentences.zh: 我们将聊聊整场革命中最让人动容的故事之一。

sentences.en: This is the fate of Marie Antoinette's son.
sentences.zh: 这就是玛丽·安托瓦内特的儿子的命运。

sentences.en: So, he's the boy, little boy, who royalists regard as Louis XVII.
sentences.zh: 也就是保王党人视之为路易十七的那个小男孩。

sentences.en: And his fate is a very, very sad story.
sentences.zh: 他的命运是一个非常、非常悲惨的故事。

sentences.en: So, don't miss it.
sentences.zh: 所以，千万不要错过。

sentences.en: Now, that's not the only episode we'll be doing.
sentences.zh: 这还不是我们要播出的唯一一期节目。

sentences.en: We'll be doing the fall of Danton.
sentences.zh: 我们还将讲述丹东的倒台。

sentences.en: We'll be doing the attack on Christianity.
sentences.zh: 我们将讲述对基督教的攻击。

sentences.en: And we'll be doing the final showdown, the climax of the reign of terror, the fall of Maximilien, Crobespiaire.
sentences.zh: 我们还将迎来最后的对决，即恐怖统治的高潮——马克西米连·罗伯斯庇尔的倒台。
zh_words: 马克西米连·罗伯斯庇尔

sentences.en: And if you want to hear all those episodes now, and you're a Rest is History club member, you can.
sentences.zh: 如果你想现在就收听所有这些节目，并且你已经是“历史的其余部分”俱乐部成员，那么你完全可以做到。

sentences.en: So, your next, you know, three or four hours are going to be brilliant.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，你接下来的三四个小时将会非常精彩。

sentences.en: If you are gutted because you're going to miss out, fear not.
sentences.zh: 如果你因为会错过而感到沮丧，别担心。

sentences.en: You can go to therestishistory.com.
sentences.zh: 你可以访问 therestishistory.com。

sentences.en: You can sign up.
sentences.zh: 你可以注册。

sentences.en: You can join the club immediately.
sentences.zh: 你可以立即加入俱乐部。

sentences.en: You'll get those episodes right away.
sentences.zh: 你马上就能听到这些节目。

sentences.en: But also, you can look forward to a whole load of supplementary benefits, the kind of thing that would make a Republican or Royalist weep with envy.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，你还可以期待一大堆额外的福利，足以让共和党人或保王党人羡慕得流泪。

sentences.en: And you could also sign up, if you like, to our newsletter, which will have loads and loads of stuff about the French Revolution, more than you could possibly want to read.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意，你也可以订阅我们的电子通讯，里面会有大量关于法国大革命的内容，绝对多到让你看不过来。

sentences.en: Surely not, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 怎么会呢，多米尼克。

sentences.en: Surely people want to read every last word of it.
sentences.zh: 大家肯定想读到关于它的每一个字。

sentences.en: It's that good.
sentences.zh: 就是这么精彩。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's actually true because it is really good.
sentences.zh: 对，这其实是真的，因为内容真的很棒。

sentences.en: So, there's loads of French Revolution content.
sentences.zh: 所以，有大量的法国大革命内容。

sentences.en: Next up, Marie Antoinette, do not miss that episode.
sentences.zh: 接下来是玛丽·安托瓦内特，千万不要错过那一期。

sentences.en: It is an absolute banger.
sentences.zh: 那绝对是一首神曲。

sentences.en: Tom, on that note, merci et au revoir.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，借此机会，谢谢你，再见。

sentences.en: Au revoir.
sentences.zh: 再见。
